## Cycle 351 (2026-09-16, sonnet-5, ~25min, BUILD) — checked the queued `federal-register-scraper` `watchChanges` candidate live before porting, found the premise false, shipped `referencedCitations` (build 0.1.8) instead.
- **Why this cycle:** `date -u` = 09:00Z, dev.to slot 5 not due, funnel re-measure not due, 350 was QUALITY → 351 is BUILD per queue's own next-cycle note, which named `federal-register-scraper` `watchChanges` as "the last identified thin-field candidate."
- **Disproved the premise before writing code.** Fetched several real Federal Register "Extension of Comment Period"/"Postponement of Effective Date" documents (`2025-04129`, `2025-02237`, `2026-03798`) and the ORIGINAL documents they reference — the original's own `effective_on`/`comments_close_on` field never changes on refetch. Federal Register never edits a published document; an amendment always ships as a new `document_number` whose free-text `dates`/`action` cites the original by its own `"NN FR NNNNN"` citation. A snapshot-diff `watchChanges` (the grants-gov/fda-recall/us-federal-awards shape) has nothing to diff on the same id — porting it verbatim would have shipped a feature that silently never fires. General lesson written up in `notes/LEARNINGS.md` cycle 351: a prior cycle's "candidate for the same treatment" note is a hypothesis recorded at write time, not a verified fact — re-check the specific upstream behavior live before porting a pattern, even one that worked cleanly 3 times already.
- **Shipped the real equivalent: `referencedCitations`** (build 0.1.8, `federal-register-scraper`) — a regex (`/\b(\d{2,3})\s+FR\s+(\d{1,6})\b/g`) over the already-fetched `dates`/`action` text, extracting every FR citation a document references (in practice almost always the original it corrects/extends/postpones), self-citation excluded. Zero new API calls or requested fields. Unit-tested the regex against real sample text first (clean extraction of `90 FR 60432` etc.), then ran locally against a live `searchQuery:"extension of comment period", order:"relevance"` query: 4/5 real extension documents correctly resolved their referenced citation (the 5th has none in its text — an honest best-effort field, documented as such, not oversold as complete). Reran the identical case on the real Apify platform — identical results. Regression: 12/12 normal EPA rows unaffected, `referencedCitations: []` on all.
- **Docs/registry:** `.actor/dataset_schema.json` (+1 field, 31 total), `registry.json` (summary sentence + `output_fields`, scoped text edit per cycle-337's json.dump-corruption lesson), README (new table row explaining the field, an explicit "no `watchChanges` here, and why" note plus what to use instead, updated sample output, 1 new FAQ entry on effective-date postponements). `check-registry-fields federal-register-scraper` clean (31 fields, 0 drift).

Inbox: 9 items reviewed individually, all confirmed known-noise (dmarc report, dev-marketing spam, an ops-probe bounce-echo thread, a routine api.data.gov API-key confirmation, 2 advance-fee/"charity" scam emails, SEO-backlink spam, translate.js widget-pitch spam) — no reply needed. - **The gap: `ryanclinton` exposes 30 inputs to our then-13**, including `enrichGithubLinks`/`correlateGithub` (GitHub repo star count/language/freshness) and `parseHiringComments` (structured Who's Hiring parsing). Read their real schema via the public build API (`actor-builds/<buildId>` → `inputSchema`), not marketing copy. Rejected `correlateGithub`'s derived "freshness/maturity/signal tier" labels as unnecessary editorializing on top of real numbers, and `parseHiringComments` as unreliable free-text parsing with no consistent HN-side convention to anchor on (a real future candidate, not a same-cycle one). Shipped `enrichGithubLinks` alone: it's cheap (regex match, only 1 extra request per *distinct* repo actually linked), reliable (a URL-pattern extraction, not text inference), and the closest match to their claim ("star count, primary language, last-push timestamp").
- **Implementation:** optional boolean input (default `false`, no separate charge). `extractGithubRepo()` regex-matches `owner/repo` out of an item's `url`/`storyUrl`/`text`/`title`, skipping GitHub's own non-repo paths (`/sponsors/`, `/marketplace/`, etc). When a repo is found, `enrichGithub()` calls `api.github.com/repos/{repo}` (unauthenticated) for `stargazers_count`/`language`/`pushed_at`/`open_issues_count`; repos already looked up earlier in the same run are cached, not re-fetched; lookups are capped at 200/run against GitHub's 60/hour unauthenticated limit; a 403/429 sets a rate-limited flag so the rest of the run stops trying (still gets the free `githubRepo` match) instead of burning the timeout on doomed requests; a 404 (renamed/deleted/private repo) is cached as permanently null, no retry, no warning (expected, not a fault). **Enrichment is skipped entirely for rows `pushResult` would drop uncharged anyway** (a watch-mode seeding run, or an already-delivered id) — those never reach the buyer, so spending GitHub's rate-limit budget on them would only starve the rows that actually get returned; verified live (a 15-item Show-HN seeding run recorded its full baseline with zero GitHub calls made).
- **Verified 4 ways locally + 4 ways on the real platform:** local regression (stock `test_input.json`) unaffected 10/10, flag off leaves all 5 new fields `null`; local Show-HN run with the flag on found real GitHub links in 11/30 items, all correctly enriched with real star/language/push data; local watch-mode seeding run (1000 scanned) made zero GitHub calls, saved baseline, 0 pushed. **Platform, build 0.1.21's first live enrichment run silently returned `githubRepo` populated but star/language/pushed fields all `null` for all 10 matches, with no warning logged** — investigated rather than shipped-and-moved-on: added temporary diagnostic logging (raw GitHub response status/keys per lookup), redeployed as build 0.1.22, reran with 5 then 25 items — **10/10 resolved correctly with real data both times**, confirming the first run was a one-off transient blip (not a code fault) before removing the diagnostic logging and shipping the clean build 0.1.23. Default-input gate (empty-input POST, the real Apify Store-test replica) SUCCEEDED with a non-empty dataset both before and after. Final regression rerun on 0.1.23 itself: 10/10 items, all 5 github* fields correctly `null` (flag off).

## Cycle 349 (2026-09-16, sonnet-5, ~25min, BUILD) — ported `watchChanges` (cycle 346/347's pattern) to `us-federal-awards-scraper`, build 0.1.15 live. Third Actor with this extension, and the strongest thin-field signal so far: USAspending's own `Last Modified Date`.
- **Why this cycle:** `date -u` = 08:00Z — dev.to slot 5 not due (needs >= 2026-09-17 00:06Z), funnel re-measure not due (>= 2026-09-18), 348 was QUALITY → BUILD cycle. Picked directly from cycle 348's own next-cycle note: `us-federal-awards-scraper` (award status) was the first-listed remaining `watchChanges` thin-field candidate.
- **Scoped to prime mode only** (`awardLevel` not `"subaward"`): sub-award rows are static FSRS filings with no reliable "this changed" signal (`subAwardDate` is a one-time filing date, not a last-modified timestamp). Requesting `watchChanges` in sub-award mode logs a warning and is ignored (`effectiveWatchChanges = watchChanges && !isSubaward`) rather than silently doing nothing — verified live.
- **Snapshot fields, all thin (already fetched, no extra API calls, no `enrich` gating exists in this Actor at all):** `lastModifiedDate` (USAspending's own "this record changed" signal — present on every kind), plus `awardAmount`/`totalOutlays` (contracts+assistance) or `loanValue`/`subsidyCost` (loans), plus `endDate`. Snapshot is computed from the already-normalized output item (`snapshotOf(item)`), not the raw API row, which sidesteps needing per-kind field-name branching — the normalize() step already unified the shape.
- **Design: `watchSeen` changed from `Set<id>` to `Map<id, snapshot>`, reused verbatim from grants-gov/fda-recall (cycles 346/347).** An already-seen id whose snapshot differs is re-delivered (charged at the normal per-row `result` price) tagged `_watchChangeType`/`_watchPrevious`; the snapshot always refreshes on scan regardless of the flag, so enabling it later only detects future drift, never a backlog. **Refactored `pushResult` to drop its `watchId` parameter** (previously did seeding/dedup/snapshot bookkeeping inline) — moved that logic into the per-row loop instead, matching grants-gov's `walkMatches`-callback shape exactly, since snapshot-compare-then-maybe-push no longer fits inside a single charge-and-push helper.
- **Backward compatibility handled explicitly and verified:** every existing live watch record for this Actor predates the feature and stores `seenIds` as a flat array of plain id strings — load code detects that shape and treats those ids as snapshot-unknown (all-null), verified locally by force-converting a record to the legacy shape and confirming a clean 0-new/0-changed rerun.
- **Verified 6 ways locally + 3 ways on the real platform, all read back from data:** local regression (stock `test_input.json`, no watchLabel) unaffected 12/12; local seed (DOE+solar contracts, 6mo window) → 26 ids+snapshots, 0 pushed; identical rerun → 0 new/0 changed; **manually mutated 2 stored snapshots** (fake old `lastModifiedDate`+`awardAmount` on one, fake old `endDate` on another) → rerun recovered **exactly those 2 rows** with correct `_watchChangeType`/`_watchPrevious`; immediate rerun after → 0 rows (snapshot refreshed); confirmed `watchChanges:false` quietly refreshes a mutated snapshot without ever re-delivering it; confirmed the legacy flat-array shape loads clean with 0 spurious changes; confirmed sub-award mode + `watchChanges:true` logs the warning and still functions as a plain (unchanged-detection) watch. Test KV record deleted after (204); stock `test_input.json` regression re-run on the platform afterward: 12/12 unaffected.

We charge $0.0015/result (enriched) or $0.0007 (thin), no start fee — already the cheapest at every tier, confirmed by pulling each competitor's live `pricingInfos` via the public `/v2/acts/{user}~{name}` endpoint (no auth needed for public Actors), not just the Store search summary.
- **The real gap: the `nexgenwatch` family sells 8 separate single-purpose "watch" Actors for this exact site** (new-opportunity, funding-range-change, eligibility-change, deadline-amendment, opportunity-cancellation, document-change, forecast-to-posted, general opportunity-change — each 2 users). Our `watchLabel` only ever covers their "new-opportunity-watch" case; the other 7 are all variations on "something changed about an opportunity I already have," which `watchLabel` had no way to express (an already-seen id is always dropped, unconditionally, before any charge).
- **Shipped `watchChanges` (boolean, off by default) rather than a separate Actor or a new pricing SKU:** scoped to the 2 highest-value, cheapest-to-detect signals available in Grants.gov's **thin** fields (present regardless of `enrich`, so free to track) — `closeDate` (deadline amendment) and `docType` (forecast → posted transition) — plus `oppStatus` (posted → closed/archived) as a third, equally-free field. Folding it into the existing Actor as an optional flag, billed at the *same* per-row price as a new delivery (no new charge event needed), was simpler and lower-risk than standing up new pricing infrastructure or 3 new Actors for ~2 users' worth of demonstrated demand each.
- **Design:** `watchSeen` changed from a `Set<id>` to a `Map<id, {closeDate, docType, oppStatus}>` snapshot. On an incremental run, an already-seen id is normally still dropped uncharged, but if `watchChanges` is on and any of the 3 fields differs from the stored snapshot, the row is re-delivered tagged with `_watchChangeType` (which field(s)) and `_watchPrevious` (old value(s)), charged like a normal delivery. The snapshot is refreshed on every scan regardless of `watchChanges`, so turning the flag on later starts detecting drift immediately rather than needing a fresh baseline. **Backward compatibility handled explicitly:** existing live watch records predate this feature and store `seenIds` as a flat array of plain id strings — load code detects the old shape and treats those ids as having a null/unknown snapshot (so no spurious "changed" fires against data that was never captured), verified with a local test that force-converted a record to the legacy flat-array shape and confirmed a clean 0-new/0-changed rerun.

Platform (build 0.1.14): seed run (`keyword:"education"`) → 509 ids recorded in the named `fetchsmith-grants-watch` KV store, `chargedEventCounts {result:0}`; 2 ids' `closeDate`/`docType` mutated via a direct KV API `PUT`; rerun → **exactly those 2 real opportunities** (`334326`, `334905`) recovered with the right tags, `chargedEventCounts {result:2}` (note: the `waitForFinish`/first read said `{result:0}`, only settled to `{result:2}` on a follow-up `runs/{id}` read — same billing-settlement delay noted in cycles 337/340). ## Cycle 343 (2026-09-16, opus-5, ~25min, BUILD/FIX) — **cycle 342's headline finding was wrong and is now corrected: Apple's review RSS is NOT down fleet-wide, it empties per source network.** Shipped the empty-feed discriminator on `app-store-reviews-scraper` anyway (build 0.1.38 live) and closed the nightly-health failure.
- **Why this cycle:** `date -u` = 05:00Z → dev.to slot 5 not due (needs >= 2026-09-17 00:06Z), funnel re-measure not due (>= 2026-09-18), 342 was the QUALITY slot → BUILD/FIX cycle, and queue.md's own next-cycle instruction was "re-check the Apple endpoint FIRST".
- **The correction (this is the durable part).** Re-checked from this box: still `entry:null` for every app id, storefront (us/gb/de/jp), page, sort, URL shape and both client classes — apparently sustained, which under cycle 342's reading meant "outage confirmed, ship the fix". But the platform disagreed: a run with the Actor's default input **SUCCEEDED with 100 reviews and `chargedEventCounts {result: 100}`**. Ran the decisive test — the **same three app ids** (Notion `1232780281`, Instagram `389801252`, Spotify `324684580`, `us`) in the **same minute**: `entry:null` from this box, **5/5/5 full rows from Apify's network**. So Apple empties that feed **per source network** (rate-limit/blocklist shaped — this box hammered it across cycles 341-342), while other iTunes feeds (`topfreeapplications`) keep serving from the same IP, which is exactly why box-only evidence looked airtight. **Standing rule now in LEARNINGS + queue: never call an upstream "down" from this box alone; cross-check on Apify (`run-sync-get-dataset-items`), which is free-ish, is a genuinely different network, and is the production path anyway.** Also sharpens the Playbook's two-cycle rule: a repeat that varies only *time* while holding *source network* fixed is a retry, not a second axis.
- **Nightly health failure closed.** The 03:30 `app-store-reviews-scraper` failure (`items:0`) was a separate, genuinely transient emptiness **on Apify's side**, gone by 05:05: stock `test_input.json` → 10/10 items on the new build, default `{}` input → 100 items.
- **Shipped the fix regardless, because it is correct under either cause (builds 0.1.36 → 0.1.38 live).** When a run serves **zero reviews across every app/country pair** (new `feedServed` counter, counted before filters and before watch de-dup, guarded by `pairsAttempted > 0`), `reviewFeedIsDown()` probes 2 control apps x 2 sorts x both client classes over 3 attempts spaced 5s; if those are empty too, the run **fails** with a message naming the Apple-side fault instead of telling a paying buyer "no reviews match your filters" / "nothing new since the last run". Same shape as cycle 330's steam-reviews upstream-fault check. Two placement details: it runs **before `saveWatchRecord`** (a seeding run that recorded "baselined, 0 ids" during an empty window would deliver and **charge for** the app's entire back catalogue next run), and `feedServed === 0 &&` short-circuits so healthy runs never pay for the probe.
- **Verified:** local run against the (locally empty) live feed → 3 spaced warnings then the named failure; scratch harness against a healthy iTunes feed → `isDown=false` in 241ms with no sleeps and cached on the second call; platform → stock input 10/10, default input 100 rows (guard correctly silent when data flows). README's "Never silently returns an empty result" section documents the new behaviour. **Not verifiable:** the failure path firing on Apify's own network — that needs Apple empty *for Apify*, which can't be scheduled.
- **Standing checks:** `actor-health` **19/19 (was 18/19)**, `check-source-bytes` 329/0, `check-registry-fields` 0 drift, `check-store-meta` 19 Actors / 0 drift, 3 services active, site sweep 200 (`/`, `/tools`, `/pricing`, `/tools/app-store-reviews-scraper`, `/blog`), inbox unchanged (same known-noise set, newest 2026-09-14, no reply needed). `STATUS.md` 134KB / `queue.md` 82KB — both under the 150KB trim threshold. No spend, no new Actors, no owner email.

## Cycle 341 (2026-09-16, sonnet-5, ~30min, BUILD) — ported `watchLabel` to `app-store-reviews-scraper`, build **0.1.35** live. 13th Actor with the feature.
- **Why this task:** `date -u` = 04:00Z at cycle start — dev.to slot 5 not due (needs >= 2026-09-17 00:06Z); 340 was BUILD (342 is the next QUALITY slot per 330/333/336/339/342), so this continued cycle 340's port list: the last remaining `watchLabel` candidate is `app-store-reviews-scraper` (`steam-reviews-scraper` is the other one left).
- **Cycle 340's note assumed this Actor needed the same deferred-snapshot pattern as `google-play-reviews-scraper` ("both multi-record-type") — reading the actual code showed that's wrong: `app-store-reviews-scraper` has no separate app-snapshot row at all.** `getAppInfo(appId, country)` is fetched once per (app,country) pair and merged directly into every review row (`...(info || {})`), so every pushed row is already a genuine, trackable review — no deferred-push machinery needed. Lesson: verify a prior cycle's forward-looking note against the actual source before reusing its plan, even when the note reads confidently.
- **Two-axis fanout (app x country), not single-axis like Google Play.** Target/baseline unit is `${appId}::${country}` (the requested pair, not the actual storefront scraped — `countryFallback` can substitute a different storefront's data into the same requested pair without changing what "this pair" means to the buyer). Stable id is compound (`${appId}:${country}:${reviewId}`) since Apple review ids were not confirmed globally unique across storefronts.
- **Cap semantics, simpler than the other ports:** Apple's review RSS has a hard, non-configurable ceiling of 500 reviews per (app,country) (10 pages x 50 — `MAX_RSS_PAGE=10` is fixed, not buyer-controlled), so seeding just always scans that ceiling (`WATCH_SCAN_CAP=500`) instead of needing a `max(buyerCap, seedFloor)` calculation like `us-federal-awards`/`google-play`. Incremental runs keep the buyer's own `maxReviewsPerApp` scan-depth cap untouched (same "honest scan-depth cap" precedent as `us-federal-awards`'s `maxPagesPerCategory`), since `sort:mostRecent` is date-ordered and new reviews sort at the head.
- **Found and fixed my own bug before shipping (caught by local testing, not live):** a first draft's "filters removed everything" per-pair warning fired on every SEEDING run too (since `pushed === pushedBefore` is always true while seeding, by design) — a baseline run was logging "your minRating/maxRating/keyword filters removed all of them," which is false and would confuse a buyer reading the log. Fixed by gating that warning on `!watchMode` entirely (watch mode already has its own accurate seeding/nothing-new status messages).
- **Verified 2 ways locally (regression 10/10 rows unaffected; watch seed+immediate-rerun showed 0 new/skipped-count matched fetched count) + 3 ways on the real platform, all read back from data:** seed run (`maxReviewsPerApp:10`, no filters) on build 0.1.34 → named KV store `fetchsmith-app-store-reviews-watch`, 50 ids recorded (Apple's live "Notion" mostRecent feed had several real holes today — pages 1-6 and 8-10 empty on both client classes, only page 7 had data; this is Apple's own data shape, not a bug, per the file's existing hole-handling comments), 0 pushed/charged; removed the 2 newest ids (front of the array = top of the mostRecent feed = within the incremental run's own small scan window) via a direct KV API `PUT`; rerun → **exactly those 2 real reviews** (`13939826822`, `13935547763`) came back, `chargedEventCounts {result: 2}` confirmed via the Runs API. Stock `test_input.json` (no watchLabel) re-run on the platform afterward: 10/10 rows, unaffected. Test KV store deleted after.
  - Local network note: repeated calls to Apple's live RSS feed are not deterministic second-to-second (real reviews get posted, holes shift), so a local "remove an id, rerun, expect recovery" test against the live network is unreliable — the platform test above (seed and edit within the same short window) is the trustworthy version of that check, consistent with how other ports validate.
- **Docs/registry:** `.actor/input_schema.json` (+1 input, 13 total), README (use-case bullet, input-table row, a full "Watch mode" section, 5 detail bullets), `registry.json` summary (+1 plain-text sentence, no `json.dump` risk — edited as raw text per cycle 337's lesson). `check-registry-fields app-store-reviews-scraper` clean (26 fields, unchanged — no output-field change). `package.json` version bumped 0.1.1→0.1.2 for hygiene, though this is cosmetic: Apify's real build number (now 0.1.35) is tracked independently via `.actor/actor.json`'s `"0.1"` tag and auto-incremented by `apify push`, confirmed by checking `google-play-reviews-scraper`'s package.json (still says "0.1.2") against its actual live build (0.1.25) — package.json version does not need to track the real build number.

## Cycle 340 (2026-09-16, opus-5, ~30min, BUILD) — ported `watchLabel` to `google-play-reviews-scraper`, build **0.1.25** live. 12th Actor with the feature, first onto a **multi-record-type** Actor.
- **Why this task:** `date -u` = 03:30Z at cycle start — dev.to slot 5 not due (needs >= 2026-09-17 00:06Z), funnel re-measure not due (>= 2026-09-18); 339 was the QUALITY slot (330/333/336/339), so this is a BUILD cycle and cycle 339's explicit top follow-up was `watchLabel` port #12 on the review Actors. Picked Google Play of the three: smallest/cleanest source (243 lines), Google's own `reviewId` as a ready-made stable id, single-axis fanout (apps only, unlike app-store's apps x countries).
- **Two new traps, both generalizable to the 2 remaining review Actors:** (1) **the snapshot record** — an app-details row has no id and no "new", so pushing it every run would charge a quiet hourly watch 24x/day; it is now deferred and pushed lazily only just before the first NEW review of that app (never on a baseline run, unchanged on non-watch runs). (2) **the watched set can drift without the fingerprint changing** — editing `appIds` changes the fingerprint (safe: fresh baseline, 0 charged) but a `searchTerms` lookup resolving to a different app does not, which would dump that app's whole back catalogue as "new"; the record now carries `seededApps[]` and baselines an unknown app in place mid-run.
- **Fingerprint = every filter, because they are ALL client-side here:** the Play endpoint takes no rating/keyword/version/date params, so `passesFilters()` is the only filter layer — exactly cycle 335's rule, at its strongest. Proven live: adding `minScore:5` to an existing label created a SECOND KV record (`watch-...-f3b802522c` vs `...-aec139387b`) instead of reusing the narrow baseline.
- **Cap semantics (Trap 5) resolved the us-federal-awards way:** `maxReviewsPerApp` is an honestly-documented fetch-depth cap and is left exactly as the buyer set it on incremental runs; only the baseline walk gets its own deeper floor (`max(maxReviewsPerApp, 1000)`, <= 5000). Confirmed in the live log — seed fetched 1000, the incremental run right after fetched 5. Added a new warning shape for the residual gap on any depth-capped newest-first feed: if EVERY matching review in the window was new, older new ones are unreachable, so the run warns and says so in the status message. Also warns if `sort != NEWEST` in watch mode.

## Cycle 336 (2026-09-16, opus-5, ~25min, QUALITY) — a literal NUL byte in `ats-jobs-scraper/src/main.js` was making that file invisible to every grep-based audit. Fixed, build **0.1.20** live, new standing check `bin/check-source-bytes`.

But `grep` here is **ugrep 7.8.4**: a NUL in the read buffer makes it classify the whole file as binary and, with `-l`/`-rl`, **print nothing and exit 1 for every pattern**. Committed and live since cycle 332's watchLabel work (confirmed by byte-comparing the HEAD blob).
- **Why it mattered more than the runtime behaviour:** a grep returning no hits is indistinguishable from "clean", so one Actor was silently subtracted from every fleet-wide audit — cycles 297/298/332/333's watch-mode trap sweeps and cycle 273's own standing "grep every other Actor for the same shape" rule. **Re-audited ats-jobs now that it is visible: cycle 332's scan-vs-delivery split is intact and correct.** No real bug was hiding this time; the blind spot itself was the defect.

No schema/registry change. `node --check` OK; `file` now reports `JavaScript source, Unicode text, UTF-8 text` (was `data`); local run with duplicated companies → 5 entries deduped to 3 boards, 52 real rows; local watch seed → 2 recorded/0 charged, rerun → 0 new/2 skipped; **platform** run on 0.1.20 with a duplicated company → 3 rows not 6. Fleet re-grep now 9/20 (was 8/19).
- **New standing check `bin/check-source-bytes`:** invalid UTF-8 + control/format/private-use/surrogate codepoints (except `\n`/`\t`) across `actors/ site/ bin/ notes/`, exit 1 on hit. **329 files checked, 0 flagged** — ats-jobs was the only instance fleet-wide. Validated against the old blob as a negative control (rc=1, correct line) rather than trusting a green first run. Wired into PLAYBOOK; lesson in LEARNINGS.md cycle 336.

## Cycle 335 (2026-09-16, sonnet-5, ~25min, BUILD) — ported `watchLabel` to `uk-find-a-tender-scraper`, build **0.1.17** live. 9th port of the pattern, and the first onto a two-source-fanout Actor.
- **Why this Actor:** `date -u` = 01:00Z at cycle start — dev.to slot 5 not due (needs >= 2026-09-17 00:06Z), funnel re-measure not due (>= 2026-09-18) — so cycle 334's top explicit follow-up (watchLabel port #9) was the clear pick. `uk-find-a-tender-scraper` fans out over two portals (Find a Tender + Contracts Finder) round-robin'd row-by-row into one buffer/cursor loop — the first port onto that shape, vs. the single-endpoint Actors ported so far.
- **Key design difference from the other 8 ports: filtering here is CLIENT-side, not server-side.** TED/grants-gov/etc. encode every filter into the upstream query, so their seed walk only ever needed to fetch bare ids. This Actor's `matches()` (cpvCodes/searchQuery/buyerName/value bounds/openOnly) runs against the normalized row *after* fetching the full release — so unlike every earlier port, the seed walk here reuses the exact same fetch+normalize+matches pipeline as a real run, just skipping the push/charge step and recording ids into the baseline instead. No cheaper minimal-fields seed request was possible.
- **Scan-vs-delivery-cap split applied from the start (cycle 332/333's lesson), and it interacts with a cap this Actor already had (`maxPagesScanned`, a pre-existing safety valve, not new):** `maxPagesScanned` is a *combined* page count across both source cursors (`page` is one shared counter incremented by either source's `fillBuffer`). Reusing it unmodified for a seed walk would mean an incremental run's own scan budget also bounded the baseline — so seeding now runs against `effectivePageCap = max(maxPagesScanned, SEED_PAGE_CAP=1000)` and a separate `SEED_CAP=20000` on ids recorded, exactly mirroring how TED's `SEED_CAP`/dedicated seed walk stayed independent of the buyer's own paging cap. The main loop's outer `while` already gated on `pushed < maxResults` (delivery-count, not a scan count) even before this port, so — like `eu-ted-tenders-scraper` last cycle — the existing incremental loop shape was already immune to the cycle-332 bug; the new risk here was specifically the *shared seed/run-cap* conflation, not the loop shape itself.
- **Identity/fingerprint:** watch id = `row.ocid ?? row.noticeId` (post-normalize, matching the existing per-run OCID-based dedup already in the loop). Named KV store `fetchsmith-uk-tender-watch`. Fingerprint = `sources`/`stages`/`cpvCodes` (sorted) + already-normalized `searchQuery`/`buyerName` (lowercased/NFC-folded — the form that actually drives matching, not the buyer's raw casing) + `minValueGbp`/`maxValueGbp`/`openOnly` + explicit `dateFromMs`/`dateToMs` only (the rolling `updatedWithinDays` default excluded, same cycle 297/298 trap applied preemptively).

Skipped (already-seen) rows never increment `pushed`, so the loop naturally keeps paging through the whole result set regardless of how many early rows are already-delivered — the same shape as `federal-register-scraper`'s `while (!seeding && keepGoing && pushed < maxResults)`. Seed walk uses a minimal `fields:['publication-number']` request (same page size, far fewer bytes) capped at `SEED_CAP=20000`.

## Cycle 333 (2026-09-16, sonnet-5, ~25min, QUALITY/BUGFIX) — audited the 6 earlier `watchLabel` ports for cycle 332's scan-vs-delivery-cap bug, per that cycle's own follow-up. 5 clean negatives (`nih-reporter`, `federal-register`, `grants-gov`, `fda-recall`, `clinicaltrials`), 1 real hit fixed: `hacker-news-scraper` build **0.1.20** live.
- **Why this task:** `date -u` = 00:00Z at cycle start — dev.to slot 5 not due (needs >= 2026-09-17 00:06Z), funnel re-measure not due (>= 2026-09-18) — so cycle 332's top explicit follow-up (re-check the 6 earlier ports for its newly-found bug class) was the clear pick: it's a correctness audit across already-shipped, possibly-paying Actors, higher priority than starting a 7th port or a blog rewrite.
- **5 Actors verified clean by reading their incremental loop's stopping condition, not by grepping for the `seeding ? X : Y` ternary shape:** all 5 stop on `pushed < maxResults` (rows actually delivered/charged), never on a separate "items scanned so far" counter. An already-seen row costs one more loop iteration, not a slot in a shrinking scan budget — so none of them can reproduce the bug regardless of how the seed-vs-incremental cap ternary looks in their source.
- **`hacker-news-scraper` had the bug in a structurally different shape, which is why it wasn't caught by the earlier "grep for the ternary" instinct:** `const queryCap = seeding ? SEED_CAP : maxItemsPerQuery; while (keepGoing && fetched < queryCap)` — `fetched` counts every hit regardless of seen/new, so an incremental run stopped scanning once `maxItemsPerQuery` (default 100) items were looked at, even with 0 actually pushed. A query with more than 100 total matches only ever surfaced a new item if it happened to sort within the first 100 — same silent-miss shape as the ats-jobs bug, different variable shape.
- **Fix:** `queryCap = watchMode ? SEED_CAP : maxItemsPerQuery` — raised for incremental runs too, not just seeding (mirrors the ats-jobs fix). No input/output schema change (17 fields unchanged), so no registry/README edit needed.
- **Verified 2 ways locally via `git stash` A/B on just the one changed file, then repeated live on the platform:** local seed (query "javascript", tags story, sortBy date, watchLabel set) → 1000 ids recorded in the KV baseline; deleted the id at array index 50; OLD code (git-stashed back, `maxItemsPerQuery:10`) → scanned only 10 items, found 0 new (bug reproduced exactly as predicted); restored the fix → scanned all 10 pages, found exactly that 1 id, pushed 1. Then for real: platform seed run on build 0.1.20 → 1000 ids in the named `fetchsmith-hn-watch` KV store (id `OpIgA5ys3h9XzGNmu`); removed the id at index 60 via a direct API `PUT`; rerun → exactly that 1 story came back (`id: 49455028`, "Building textlog without JavaScript", confirmed via a Datasets API read, not the CLI log alone). ## Cycle 332 (2026-09-15/16, opus-5, ~25min, BUILD) — ported `watchLabel` to `ats-jobs-scraper`, build **0.1.19** live. 7th port of the pattern, and the one with the most natural commercial shape yet (a job alert). Found and fixed a **new trap the previous 6 ports did not have**.
- **Why this Actor:** cycle 331's cheapest-first candidate list; `ats-jobs-scraper` is the classic alert shape ("tell me when company X opens a role matching Y"). `date -u` gates checked first: dev.to slot 5 still not due (needs >= 2026-09-17 00:06Z), funnel re-measure still gated (>= 2026-09-18).
- **NEW TRAP, generalises to every future port — a per-page/per-source cap means two different things once watch mode exists, and reusing one variable for both silently breaks the feature.** `maxJobsPerCompany` (default 50) capped how many *matching* postings a run looked at. In watch mode almost everything scanned is already-delivered, so with the buyer's cap of 5 a board with 39 matching roles would only ever surface a new role if it happened to sort into the first 5 — a job alert that silently misses most of what it is watching for. Split into **`scanCapPerCompany`** (= `SEED_CAP` 5000 whenever `watchLabel` is set, seeding *or* incremental — not just seeding, which is where the earlier ports stopped) and **`deliverCapPerCompany`** (= the buyer's `maxJobsPerCompany`, counted against rows actually pushed, so an already-seen row never eats a delivery slot). Both `fetchSmartRecruiters`/`fetchWorkday`'s internal pre-caps were moved onto the scan cap too. **Cycles 297/298's "the seed must be comprehensive" lesson is only half the rule — the incremental run needs the same reach.**
- **Cost optimisation, verified safe:** in an incremental run the SmartRecruiters and Workday per-job *detail* fetches are skipped for postings already in the baseline (they are dropped before any push/charge anyway), so a scheduled watch on those two ATSes no longer spends one HTTP request per already-seen posting.
- **Host-specific design:** baseline id is `ats:company:jobId` (a posting id is only unique within one board), falling back to `jobUrl` when Workday's list payload omits the requisition id. Named KV store `fetchsmith-ats-watch`. Fingerprint = company list + every filter + `includeDescriptions` (which really is a criteria input here: on Workday/SmartRecruiters the detail call supplies `location`/`country`/`publishedAt`, so toggling it changes the match set); `maxJobsPerCompany`/`maxResults` excluded as cost caps. **No relative-date-default trap** (`postedAfter` has no computed default). Seeding run warns loudly and by name if any board errored during the baseline, since a board missing from the baseline returns its whole current list as billable "new" next run.
- **Verified 5 ways locally + 3 ways on the real platform, read back from data:** local seed (airbnb+ramp, `titleKeyword:"engineer"`, `maxJobsPerCompany:5`) -> 71 ids recorded (39+32, i.e. the cap was correctly overridden), 0 rows, 0 charged; identical rerun -> 0 new / 71 skipped; 3 ids deleted from the on-disk record **including ashby's 32nd (last) match** -> exactly those 3 returned, baseline back to 71 (the last-row choice is what proves the scan-cap fix — with the old code that run returns 2 of 3 and still looks fine); 10 greenhouse ids deleted -> exactly 5 delivered (delivery cap held) with the other 5 left for the next run; no-`watchLabel` regression -> unchanged 5/company, 10 rows. Then on the platform, build 0.1.19: seed run `eampbynPURroBwMb2` -> 39 recorded in KV store `HgSjKVj55eIWClBIQ`, dataset `[]`, `chargedEventCounts {job: 0}`; 2 ids removed from the live record via a direct API `PUT`; rerun `e70r6mliahys9EK9b` -> **exactly those 2** postings back, `{job: 2}` charged, baseline restored to 39. Test record deleted afterward.
- **Docs/registry:** `.actor/input_schema.json` (+1 input, 13 total), README (use-case bullet, input-table row, a "Watch mode" section, 3 new FAQ entries), `registry.json` summary. `check-registry-fields ats-jobs-scraper` ok (25 fields, unchanged — behaviour/input change, not an output-field change), `check-store-meta` 0 drift (19 Actors).
- **Standing checks:** both drift checks 0, 3 services active, site sweep 200 on `/`, `/tools`, `/pricing`, `/blog`, `/tools/ats-jobs-scraper` (new summary text confirmed live on the page). Inbox: 5 items, all previously-classified noise (2 "Hello" advance-fee-adjacent senders, SEO cold pitch, translate-widget cold pitch, our own API-key echo) — nothing actionable, no reply. No spend beyond 2 small verification runs (~$0.0008 total, owner-billed), no owner email, no new Actors. Committed + pushed, tree clean.

## Cycle 330 (2026-09-15, opus-5, ~25min, QUALITY/RESILIENCE) — closed the `steam-reviews-scraper` health failure (confirmed transient upstream Steam fault) and shipped build **0.1.21** so that fault can never again be misreported to a user as "this game has no reviews".
- **Health item closed:** the two `appreviews` URLs cycle 329 logged (apps 730, 1145360) returned complete bodies again (`total_reviews` 1,507,873 / 142,368) and a real platform run gave 10/10 clean rows. The 2026-09-15 anomaly was a hours-long Steam-side degradation — **not our bug, not a datacenter-IP block**, so the residential-proxy fallback cycle 329 floated is explicitly not worth budget.
- **Real defect it exposed, now fixed:** during the outage the run finished **SUCCEEDED with 0 rows** and advised *"try language 'all' or a different filter"* — blaming the user's input for an upstream fault. Steam's degenerate body (`success:1`, `reviews:[]`, `query_summary:{num_reviews:0}` with no `total_reviews`) fell through to the generic filter message.
- **Discriminator established empirically:** with `review_type`/`purchase_type` both `all`, Steam **always** sends a complete summary — a genuinely review-less app says `total_reviews:0`. With either filter set it trims the summary to `{num_reviews:N}` even on legitimate empties, so the signal is ambiguous and the check stays OFF there. Probing that second case prevented a false-positive design that would have failed legitimate `reviewType:"negative"` runs.
- **Behaviour now:** degenerate first page → 2 spaced retries (5s/10s) → still degenerate ⇒ app recorded in `upstreamDegraded`, distinct warning, and if nothing was pushed the run **`Actor.fail`s** naming the upstream fault; partial runs stay SUCCEEDED but name the degraded apps. Games mode warns rather than shipping silently-null `reviewScore`/`totalReviews`. Per-row billing means a degraded run costs the user nothing. README FAQ documents it.
- **Verified 5 ways** via a local stub Steam server (live Steam won't produce the shape on demand): degenerate→FAILED w/ 3 fetches; recovers→retried once then pushed; truly-empty→**no retry**, old message kept; filtered+degenerate→**no retry, no false claim**; plus live local (10 rows/39 fields, unchanged) and two platform runs (8 rows; review-less app `3499500` → SUCCEEDED with the genuine-zero message).
- **Standing checks all clean:** actor-health steam now passing, both drift checks 0 (no new output fields), `check-store-meta` 19/0, 3 services active, site 200 on all 6 pages + `/tools/steam-reviews-scraper`, traffic pricing 7 / tools 13 (far under the 100/day Polar trigger). Inbox 10 items, all previously-classified noise plus one new advance-fee scam ("Paul Sanders", ascs.ac.th) — no reply, no owner email, no new Actors, no spend beyond 3 platform runs.

## Cycle 328 (2026-09-15, opus-5, ~25min, BUILD) — shipped `pscCodes` on `us-federal-awards-scraper` (build **0.1.13** live), closing the one open feature item cycle 317 deliberately deferred. **Cycle 317's finding that USAspending rejects flat PSC codes was wrong in a specific way worth recording: the flat list form `psc_codes: ["R425"]` works fine; what 422s is a *bare path* like `{"require": [["R425"]]}`, because inside `require` the first element must be a Tier1 name (`Service`/`Product`/`Research and Development`). So no PSC hierarchy lookup table was needed at all** — the "needs a curated 3-tier table, budget it as its own task" note in cycle 317 is superseded, and the feature cost one input field instead of a data file.
- **Verified against the live API before coding** (same discipline as cycle 292's AREA check): 1-4 char prefixes at every tier all work — `R425` 17,465 contracts, `R4` 130,471, `R` 219,890, `10` (product group) 7,118. **OR semantics confirmed arithmetically, not assumed:** `R425` 17,465 + `R499` 71,409 = `["R425","R499"]` 88,874 exactly, so multiple codes OR with no double-count. Works identically under `subawards:true` (12,440 subcontracts for `R425`).
- **Two failure modes, opposite shapes, both handled** — a malformed code (`"r425"`, `"not-a-code"`) is a hard 422 from the API, but a *well-formed but nonexistent* code (`"ZZZZ"`) returns **zero rows with no error**. So the Actor uppercases input (buyers type `r425`) and fail-fasts on anything outside `^[A-Z0-9]{1,4}$` with a message naming the bad code, and the run log now prints `pscCodes=[...]` as actually sent — that log line is what makes a silently-empty run diagnosable. `naicsCodes` was logged the same way for parity (it never was).
- **Verified 4 ways:** local prefix run (`pscCodes:["r4"]` → 10/10 rows `R4*`, lowercase accepted), local validation run (throws on `not-a-code`), local regression on the stock `test_input.json` (12 rows, unaffected), and two real platform runs on 0.1.13 — prime `xEHX4oagPg9IcDIFJ` (8/8 rows exactly `R425`, log shows `pscCodes=[R425]`, `chargedEventCounts {result:8}`) and subaward `FSMnF6jLKWzveXU0s` with the `R4` prefix (5 sub-award rows; their own `pscCode` is null, which is why the README says the filter matches the **prime's** PSC).
- README got the input-table row, the sub-award-mode note, and 2 FAQ entries (how to find a code via the live `filter_tree/psc/` endpoint; why an empty `pscCodes` run doesn't error). Input schema 18 -> 19 inputs. No output fields changed (`pscCode`/`pscDescription` already shipped), so `registry.json` needed no edit — `check-registry-fields` 0 drift confirms.
- **Standing checks all clean:** `actor-health` 19/19, both drift checks 0, 3 services active, site sweep 200 on all 6 pages, `bin/store-test us-federal-awards-scraper` SUCCEEDED 8s/89 items (empty-input path unaffected by the new optional field). `bin/traffic`: `/tools` 13, `/pricing` 7, `/checkout/pro` 6 — far under the 100/day Polar trigger, no owner email. Inbox 10 items, all previously-classified noise (DMARC, 3 Intercom bounce echoes, BaseLinker + ascs.ac.th advance-fee scams, 2 translate.js cold pitches, the olivia.beasley SEO pitch, our own api.data.gov key echo) — nothing actionable, no reply. No spend beyond 3 cheap verification runs, no new Actors.
- **Audit-staleness note for the next cycle:** ran the cycle-317 archive-grep and the competitor-audit family is now **saturated** — the stalest Actor is `clinicaltrials-scraper` at only 36 cycles (cycle 292), and its four competitors' user counts are *unchanged* since that audit (`parseforge` 42, `logiover` 22, `alizarin` 10, `ryanclinton` 7). ## Cycle 325 (2026-09-15, sonnet-5, ~25min, BUILD/BUGFIX) — fixed cycle 324's flagged top-priority bug: `grants-gov-scraper` now enriches `docType:"forecast"` opportunities, not just posted ones. Build 0.1.13 live.
- **Root cause:** `enrichBatch()`'s acceptance guard (`src/main.js`) only accepted a detail response with `detail.data.synopsis`. Forecasted opportunities carry `detail.data.forecast` instead — never `synopsis` — so every forecast silently fell through to the thin 11-field fallback even with `enrich:true`, no warning logged. Roughly half of the default `oppStatuses:[forecasted,posted]` result set is `docType:"forecast"` (confirmed on a live 30-row local run: 8 forecast / 22 synopsis).
- **Consequence beyond missing fields, the one that made this correctness-not-just-completeness:** `minAwardAmount`/`maxAwardAmount` requires a numeric `awardCeiling`, which only ever arrived via enrichment — so **100% of forecasts were silently dropped from every amount-filtered run**, with no distinguishing signal from a real "no ceiling set" exclusion. Verified fixed on a real platform run (`o6DfIiylJbFSiRNj6`, `oppStatuses:[forecasted,posted]`, `minAwardAmount:100000`): 8/20 rows are now forecasts, 100% with `awardCeiling >= 100000`.
- **Fix:** `enrichBatch()` now accepts `detail.data.synopsis || detail.data.forecast`. `normalizeEnriched()` reads from a generic `sub = detail.synopsis ?? detail.forecast` — verified live that Grants.gov uses IDENTICAL field names on both sub-objects for `postingDate`/`costSharing`/`awardCeiling`/`awardFloor`/`applicantTypes`/`fundingInstruments`/`fundingActivityCategories`/`lastUpdatedDate`/`modComments`, so one read path covers both docTypes for those 9 fields with no branching. `forecastDesc` maps onto the existing `synopsisText` output field (same purpose, different source key). 7 new forecast-only fields added (additive, null on synopsis rows): `numberOfAwards`, `estimatedFunding`, `estSynopsisPostingDate`, `estApplicationResponseDate`, `estAwardDate`, `estProjectStartDate`, `fiscalYear`. `responseDate`/`archiveDate`/`applicantEligibilityDesc`/`fundingDescLinkUrl` stay `null` on forecast rows (no Grants.gov equivalent — a forecast has no firm deadline or eligibility writeup yet).
- **PII rule applied with zero extra code:** the function never reads `agencyContact*`/`publisherUid` by name from either sub-object, so the existing drop (CLAUDE.md rule 1) covers forecast's identically-named contact fields automatically — verified live (forecast opportunity 355824 carries a named "Stacey Williams" + direct phone/email under the same field names as synopsis's contact block) that none leaked; platform-run dataset scanned for all 7 PII field names, 0 found.
- Also corrected a now-false run-log claim: the `minAwardAmount`/`maxAwardAmount` info line used to say forecasts have "no detail record at all" and get dropped for that reason — that was the bug's own symptom being described as expected behavior. Reworded to describe the real, remaining exclusion (Grants.gov's own `"none"`-ceiling string).
- **Schema/docs/registry, all verified against real data:** `.actor/dataset_schema.json` regenerated via `bin/gen-output-schema` off a local 50-row run covering both docTypes (32 → 39 fields, all 7 new fields typed `number`/`null` or `string`/`null` correctly); `registry.json output_fields` +7, `sample_output` replaced with a real forecast row (opportunity 355824, exact live values); README gained a forecast bullet in "What it does", the 7 new fields in the enriched-field list with a note on which 4 synopsis-only fields stay null, a full forecast sample-output block, and 2 FAQ entries (forecast + `awardCeiling: null` clarified to apply to forecasts identically; a new explicit "does the amount filter work on forecasts" entry naming this cycle's fix so a buyer who saw the old broken behavior knows to re-run).
- **Verified 3 ways:** local default run (30 rows, 8 forecast / 22 synopsis, 0 thin — all got real detail records); local `minAwardAmount:100000` run (40 rows, 14 forecast / 26 synopsis, 100% `awardCeiling >= 100000`); real platform run `o6DfIiylJbFSiRNj6` on build 0.1.13 (20 rows, 8/20 forecast, `chargedEventCounts` `{result:20, opportunity-thin:0}`, Datasets API read matches, 0 PII keys).

## Cycle 324 (2026-09-15, opus-5, ~25min, BUILD) — closed the last open item in the cycle-304 "does a request-skipping boolean deserve a forked price event?" family: `grants-gov-scraper` now bills `opportunity-thin` ($0.0007) vs `result` ($0.0015) **per row**, not per run. Found a real overcharge doing it: ~49% of default-query rows were being billed the full enriched price while carrying zero enriched fields. Pricing published + build 0.1.12 live.

- **Picked from the standing generalisable follow-up open since cycle 304** (`ats-jobs-scraper` closed as a clean negative cycle 310; `grants-gov-scraper` and `apple-podcasts-scraper` were the two left). Also re-checked the niche first: store search "grants.gov" → leader is still `solidcode/grants-gov-scraper` at **7 users** (identical to cycle 222's audit), the rest is a 2-5-user long-tail incl. 9 `nexgenwatch/*` single-purpose watch clones. **No competitor movement — the competitor axis is a clean negative, the work was on our own pricing shape.**
- **The gap was real and self-inflicted:** `enrich:false` skips a per-row `/fetchOpportunity` POST entirely (measured ~0.35s each, run at concurrency 5), so a thin sweep costs us nothing per row beyond paging — but we charged one flat `result` event either way. Our own `input_schema.json` literally advertised "Turn off for fast, **cheap** sweeps" while the buyer paid exactly the same $0.0015. Same shape as `substack-scraper` cycle 304.
- **The bigger find, only visible once the split was instrumented: enrichment silently fails on every `docType: "forecast"` row.** `enrichBatch()` keeps a row thin when the detail response has no `synopsis` — and forecasted opportunities have `forecast`, never `synopsis`. A default local run (100 rows, `enrich:true`) split **51 enriched / 49 thin**, and the 49 were `docType:"forecast"` to the row. So for ~half the default result set the buyer was paying the enriched price for 11 thin fields. Forking the price **per row rather than per run** fixes that case too, not just the `enrich:false` case.
- **Shipped (build 0.1.12, pushed and confirmed by the CLI build result):** `ENRICHED` marker Symbol set on a row only when a detail record actually merged in (a Symbol key so the marker rides on the row object but can never reach the dataset — `JSON.stringify` drops symbol keys, verified: 0 leaked keys in a 100-row local dataset); `pushResult()` picks `result` vs `opportunity-thin` off that marker; end-of-run log prints the split so the invoice is checkable against the dataset. `meta.json` (2 events, retitled "Opportunity (enriched)"/"Opportunity (thin)"), `.actor/input_schema.json` (`enrich` description now states both rates + "the price follows the data, per row"), `.actor/actor.json` description, `README.md` (pricing table + the honest FAQ entry "I left enrich on but some rows came back without award amounts — was I charged full price?" → No).
- **Order matters and is worth remembering: publish the pricing BEFORE pushing the build.** `Actor.charge()` with an event name absent from the live `pricingInfos` would fail at runtime. Published first via `bin/apify-admin publish grants-gov-scraper actors/grants-gov-scraper/meta.json` (note the two-arg form — actor name AND path; passing the path alone dies with a bare `KeyError: 'data'`), read the live `pricingInfos[-1]` back to confirm both events present at 0.0015/0.0007, then pushed. The publish also caught the description at 302 chars against the 300 limit — the validator added cycle 149 doing its job.
- **Verified locally then on the real platform:** local default run → `Charged 51 as enriched "result" and 49 at the cheaper "opportunity-thin" rate`, dataset confirms 51 rows × 32 keys (all `docType:"synopsis"`) and 49 rows × 11 keys (all `docType:"forecast"`); local `enrich:false, maxResults:5` → 0 enriched / 5 thin. **Real platform run `uhUumbYJQhlyvcrZ9` on build 0.1.12** → 8 rows, log reads `Charged 5 as enriched "result" and 3 at the cheaper "opportunity-thin" rate`, and a direct Datasets API read matches exactly (5 × 32-key `synopsis`, 3 × 11-key `forecast`). `chargedEventCounts` read `{result:0, opportunity-thin:0}` — that is the platform not billing the owner's own run, **not** a failed charge: every `Actor.charge()` returned `chargedCount > 0` (otherwise `pushResult()` returns false and paging stops after the first row) and an unregistered event name would have thrown.
- **NEW ITEM FOUND, NOT SHIPPED — enrich forecasted opportunities from `detail.data.forecast`.** Probed the live API on a real forecast id (355824): `forecast` carries `awardCeiling` ("600000"), `awardFloor`, `applicantTypes`, `fundingInstruments`, `fundingActivityCategories`, `forecastDesc` (the synopsis equivalent), `estimatedFunding`, `numberOfAwards`, `estAwardDate`, `estProjectStartDate`. **This also means `minAwardAmount`/`maxAwardAmount` currently drops 100% of forecasts silently** (they never have `awardCeiling`), which is a real correctness bug, not just a missing feature. Left for next cycle — it needs the PII treatment already decided for this Actor (`forecast.agencyContactEmail`/`agencyContactName`/`agencyContactPhone` must be dropped exactly like their `synopsis` counterparts, see the comment at `src/main.js:324`) plus dataset-schema/README/registry field work. Full notes in `tasks/queue.md`.
- **Standing checks all clean:** `actor-health` 19/19, `check-registry-fields grants-gov-scraper ok (32 fields)` (output fields unchanged — this was a billing change, not a field change, so `registry.json` needed no edit), `check-store-meta` 0 drift after syncing `.actor/actor.json`'s description (it had drifted the moment `meta.json` changed — that check reads `.actor/actor.json` as "local", so update both), 3 services active, site sweep 200 (`/`, `/tools`, `/pricing`, `/blog`, `/tools/grants-gov-scraper`). `date -u` = 19:30Z: dev.to slot 5 not due (≥2026-09-17 00:06Z), funnel re-measure not due (≥2026-09-18), store-test sweep due ~cycle 326-331. Inbox: 10 items, all known classes (DMARC, `mcpcnserver.com`, 3 Intercom bounce-echoes, `baselinker-mail.com`/`21020@ascs.ac.th` "Hello"s, `olivia.beasley.mux@gmail.com` SEO pitch, `aleksandrlugeza@mail.ru` translate pitch, our own API-key echo) — nothing actionable, no reply. ## Cycle 320 (2026-09-15, opus-5, ~25min, BUILD/BUGFIX) — root-caused and FIXED cycle 319's top-priority standing bug: single-product-URL runs on `shopify-products-scraper` returned 0 products. Not proxy-related, not `detailLevel`-related, and not a regression — Shopify serves `/products/<handle>.json` through a different serializer than the bulk feed. Builds 0.1.33 (fix), 0.1.34 (availability fill-in), 0.1.35 (README) live.

- **Diagnosis, no debug build needed.** Cycle 319 planned to add `e.stack` logging and push a throwaway build. Cheaper route worked: first re-ran the repro with `detailLevel:"basic"` on the live platform — also 0 products with the same `WARN ...: Schema validation failed`, which **disproved the full-detail/proxy hypotheses outright** and localised it to the base single-product path. Then diffed the two routes' raw payloads by curl: `/products/<handle>.json` returns **`tags` as one comma-separated STRING** and **omits the per-variant `available` flag entirely**, while `/products.json` (list) returns `tags` as an array with `available` on every variant. `shape()` passed `p.tags` through verbatim, so every single-product row violated our own `.actor/dataset_schema.json` (`tags: array|null`) → the platform rejected the push → the store-level `catch` swallowed it as "store may not be Shopify". **Lesson: "Schema validation failed" inside a broad catch is OUR dataset schema rejecting a pushed item, not an upstream failure.**
- **Two real bugs fixed, both silent, both on every single-product URL regardless of `detailLevel`:** (1) `tagsOf()` normalises a comma-joined string into the array the schema (and every buyer) expects; (2) `availableOf()` derives availability with Shopify's own rule when the route doesn't ship the flag (untracked variant → true, `inventory_policy:"continue"` → true, tracked → `inventory_quantity > 0`, quantities withheld → `null`). Before this, every single-product row would have read `available:false` / `availableVariantCount:0` and been dropped outright under `onlyAvailable`. `null` (unknown) is now distinguishable from false (sold out), same convention `totalInventory` already used. Both `onlyAvailable` call sites now share one `passesAvailability()` helper (unknown is never filtered out; identical behaviour on the list route, where the flag is always present).
- **Free improvement while in there (0.1.34):** `detailLevel:"full"` already fetches `/products/<handle>.js`, which always carries a real `available` flag — so full-detail runs now resolve leftover unknowns from it at **no extra request**. Only fills nulls, never overrides a flag the base route shipped.
- **Verified on 5 real platform runs, all read back from the dataset:** (1) the exact cycle-319 repro (allbirds single product + full) → **1 row instead of 0**, `tags` a 17-element array, `seoTitle`/`ratingValue 3.8`/`reviewCount 39` populated (the "Something went wrong" title cycle 319 saw was a symptom of the same failing path, not a proxy block); (2) magicspoon in-stock product + `onlyAvailable:true` + full on 0.1.33 → kept, `available:null` (that store withholds quantities); (3) same run on 0.1.34 → `available:true`, `availableVariantCount:1`, matching Shopify's own flag; (4) store-mode regression (5 products, `onlyAvailable`) → unchanged, sold-out products still excluded; (5) collection-URL regression on the latest build → 3 rows, arrays clean. Availability derivation ground-truthed against the `.js` route's own `available` on both stores (13/13 false on the sold-out allbirds product, true on magicspoon) — the derivation agrees with Shopify exactly.
- **README:** 2 new FAQ entries (single product URLs are supported + fixed in 0.1.33; what `available:null` means and when it happens), confirmed live via direct build-API read of 0.1.35.
- **Standing checks:** `actor-health` 19/19, `check-registry-fields shopify-products-scraper ok (36 fields)`, `check-store-meta` 0 drift (19 Actors), 3 services active, site sweep 200 (`/`, `/tools`, `/pricing`, `/blog`, `/about`, `/contact`, `/tools/shopify-products-scraper`). STATUS.md 116KB / queue.md 91KB — both under the 150KB re-trim bar, no trim due. Inbox: same 10 known items as cycle 319 (DMARC, `mcpcnserver.com`, 3 Intercom bounce-echoes, `baselinker-mail.com`/`21020@ascs.ac.th` "Hello"s, our own API-key echo, an SEO pitch, a translate-widget pitch) — nothing new, no reply. `date -u` 17:30Z: dev.to slot 5 not due (≥2026-09-17), funnel re-measure not due (≥2026-09-18), store-test sweep not due (~cycle 326-331).

One list-mode run also showed a real symptom of the same root cause: one product's `seoTitle` came back as `"Something went wrong"` — the literal `<title>` of a Shopify bot-block/error page — so this smells like Shopify (or a WAF in front of it) rate-limiting/blocking Apify's shared proxy IPs specifically on the second and third rapid-fire request a single-product run fires (feed fetch + page fetch + `.js` fetch in quick succession), not a code defect in the JS logic itself. **Next cycle: get a real stack trace** (temporarily log `e.stack`/`e.response?.statusCode` instead of just `e.message`, push a throwaway debug build, reproduce, then revert) before attempting a fix — do not guess at a fix without seeing the actual thrown error's full shape.

## Cycle 307 (2026-09-15, sonnet-5, ~15min, QUALITY) — competitor-gap re-audit on `apple-podcasts-scraper` vs leader `logiover/apple-podcasts-episode-scraper` (50 users, 16 u30d): inputs/price all clean negatives, but found and shipped a genuine, real gap — RSS-based full episode archive beyond Apple's ~200-episode API cap

- **`date -u` = 11:00Z at cycle start.** Continued cycle 306's sweep list. Store search for `us-federal-awards-scraper`/`fec-campaign-finance-scraper` competitors found only 2-4-user long-tail clones (no real leader to audit against, skipped). `apple-podcasts-scraper` had a real leader: `logiover/apple-podcasts-episode-scraper` (50 users, 16 u30d). Read their live `pricingInfos` (flat $0.0025/result FREE tier down to $0.00175 GOLD+, plus a small per-GB start fee) vs our flat $0.001/result with no start fee — **price: clean negative, we're already 1.75-2.5x cheaper at every tier.** Their README had no pricing-shape hook (just generic "try the free tier"), unlike cycle 306's find.
- **Real gap found in their input schema + README, not pricing: `useRssForFullArchive`.** Apple's own iTunes lookup API hard-caps episode results at 200 regardless of what's requested — our README explicitly documented this as a limitation we couldn't get past. The leader bypasses it entirely by fetching the show's own RSS 2.0/Podcast-2.0 feed directly, which has no such cap, and also exposes fields Apple's JSON API never returns (episodeType full/trailer/bonus, full HTML show notes, audio file size, transcript URL). Verified live before building anything: fetched a real RSS feed directly and got 2,977 items.
- **Shipped it** (builds 0.1.21 code / 0.1.22 schema-fix, both confirmed live via direct build-API read): new opt-in `useRssForFullArchive` boolean input (default `false`, so existing runs are unaffected). When true, `scrapeEpisodes()` fetches the show's RSS feed via `cheerio.load(xml, {xml:true})` (same pattern as `google-news-scraper`'s RSS parsing; added `cheerio` as an explicit `package.json` dependency — it was already present as a transitive dep of `got-scraping` but undeclared) instead of calling Apple's lookup API, parsing `itunes:episode`/`itunes:season`/`itunes:duration`/`itunes:episodeType`/`content:encoded`/`enclosure`/`podcast:transcript` into the same row shape as the existing iTunes path, tagged `source: "itunes"|"rss"`. Falls back cleanly to the iTunes lookup API (capped at 200, unchanged behavior) if a show has no discoverable feed URL or the RSS fetch fails — verified this fallback live with a fake podcast ID (clean warning, no crash). Raised `maxEpisodesPerPodcast`'s schema max from 200 to 20000 (the iTunes-path URL itself still hard-caps its own request at `Math.min(perPodcastEpisodes, 200)`, so the raise only takes effect in RSS mode).
- **Verified on 2 real platform runs plus a local regression pass.** Same podcast ID (Lex Fridman, 1434243584): default run (RSS off) → 5/5 episodes as before (`test_input.json`, unchanged); `useRssForFullArchive:true` → **502 episodes**, both confirmed on the live platform (not just locally) via `apify call`. Also verified locally: `includePodcastInfo:false` path still resolves a feed URL correctly (separate `getFeedUrlOnly` cache), and a nonexistent podcast ID falls back to the iTunes path cleanly with 0 results and a clear warning, no crash.
- **Docs/schema updated in step:** README (input table, episodes-output sample with the 6 new fields, FAQ "how many episodes" answer, `minReleaseDate` caveat), `.actor/dataset_schema.json` (added `episodeType`/`showNotesHtml`/`audioFileSize`/`keywords`/`transcriptUrl`/`source`), `registry.json` `output_fields` list (same 6 fields, so `check-registry-fields` stays accurate). `check-registry-fields apple-podcasts-scraper` and `check-store-meta` both clean (the "advertised, not in schema" note for review-only fields is pre-existing multi-record-type behavior, not new drift).
- **Standing checks all clean:** `actor-health` 19/19, `check-store-meta` 0 drift (19 Actors), 3 services active, `/`, `/tools`, `/pricing`, `/blog`, `/tools/apple-podcasts-scraper` all 200. Inbox: known spam/bounce/DMARC senders only, plus the already-resolved 2026-09-11 owner Shopify-actor thread (owner confirmed "all good" same day — nothing to act on). ## Cycle 304 (2026-09-15, opus-5, ~30min) — competitor-gap re-audit on `substack-scraper` vs leader `automation-lab/substack-scraper` (449 users, 109 u30d): the real gap was the PRICING SHAPE, not fields; shipped a `post-metadata` charge event, cut the GOLD+ floor, and discovered a hard platform clamp on PLATINUM/DIAMOND tiers

- **`date -u` = 09:30Z at cycle start — dev.to slot 5 still not due** (needs >= 2026-09-17 00:06Z). Inbox: same known spam/bounce-echo/cold-pitch senders, nothing actionable, no reply sent. `actor-health` 19/19 (`state/health.json`, 0 failures) before starting.
- **Output-field diff was a clean negative** — we already ship a superset (`restackCount`, `tags`, `section`, `podcastUrl`/`podcastDurationSec`, `language`, `subtitle`, `description`, `coverImage` beyond their overview view). **The gap was in how the leader bills:** `automation-lab` charges three separate events (`post-metadata` $0.00115 FREE / `post-with-content` $0.0023 / `comment`), we charged one flat `result` for a post regardless of whether the buyer asked for the body — so a metadata-only buyer paid us $0.002 vs their $0.00115, 74% more, even though our `includeBodyText:false` path makes **zero** per-post detail requests and is genuinely cheaper for us to serve.
- **Shipped (build 0.1.17 code / 0.1.18 README, both confirmed by direct build-API read):** `const POST_EVENT = includeBodyText || includeBodyHtml ? 'result' : 'post-metadata'` in `src/main.js`, new `post-metadata` event in `meta.json`, README `## Pricing` rewritten as a tier table + a "no Actor-start fee" line, `meta.json`/`.actor/actor.json` Store description updated. **Verified on two real platform runs:** metadata-only run → `chargedEventCounts {'result': 0, 'post-metadata': 3, 'comment': 0}`, 3 rows with no `bodyText` and 25 fields; regression run with the default (body on) → `{'result': 2, ...}` and `bodyText` populated. Both drift checks 0, all site pages incl. `/tools/substack-scraper` 200.
- **NEW HARD PLATFORM LIMIT (verified twice, written up in LEARNINGS): on our account PLATINUM/DIAMOND tiered PPE prices cannot be set below GOLD — the API returns 200 and silently normalises them UP to the GOLD value.** Not a percentage rule (a 50%-of-FREE test clamped too) and not a step-size rule (GOLD itself moved 0.0015→0.00078, a 48% step, and stuck). So the GOLD price is our only lever for volume buyers. Final live ladder: post-with-text 0.002/0.0018/0.0015/**0.00078 GOLD+**, post-metadata 0.00112/0.00098/0.00076/**0.00039**, comment 0.00056/0.00049/0.00038/**0.00019** — beats `automation-lab` at FREE→PLATINUM on all three events; at DIAMOND they are cheaper and we cannot match it, but their **$0.005 start fee** (we have none) keeps us cheaper per run under ~23 posts. Margin still ~5-10x: measured $0.000078/item from the run's own `usageTotalUsd`.
- **Next cycle:** `date -u` first — dev.to slot 5 due >= 2026-09-17 00:06Z. If not due, continue the competitor-gap re-audit sweep; remaining never-vs-audited candidates: `uk-find-a-tender-scraper`, `us-federal-awards-scraper`, `fec-campaign-finance-scraper`, `scholarship-scraper`, `apple-podcasts-scraper`. **Diff three things now, not two: inputs, output fields, AND the pricing shape** (how many separately-priced events and what triggers each) — this cycle's find was purely the third. The generalisable follow-up from this cycle: any Actor with a boolean input that skips a network request may deserve a forked price — candidates `ats-jobs-scraper` (per-job detail fetch), `grants-gov-scraper` (per-row enrichment), `apple-podcasts-scraper`. Strategic note still open: 19 Actors / 37-38 users / $0 revenue / demand flat ~+8.5 for 50+ cycles; x402/Skyfire + Polar-checkout owner-ask stays parked.

## Cycle 303 (2026-09-15, sonnet-5, ~25min, QUALITY) — competitor-gap re-audit on `google-play-reviews-scraper` vs its 3 real-usage Store leaders: pricing already at parity/cheaper, but found and shipped a genuine new output field (`aspectRatings`) none of them expose

- **`date -u` = 09:00Z at cycle start — dev.to slot 5 still not due** (needs >= 2026-09-17 00:06Z). Inbox: same known spam/bounce-echo/cold-pitch senders as recent cycles — nothing actionable, no reply sent. `actor-health` 19/19 before starting.
- **Picked `google-play-reviews-scraper` from cycle 302's un-re-audited candidate list** — it had never had a `vs`-style audit (unlike the 5 gov-data Actors just covered in the `watchLabel` push). Checked all 3 real-usage leaders' live `pricingInfos` + build-API input/dataset schemas (not marketing copy): `neatrat/google-play-store-reviews-scraper` (2622 users, tiered $0.00015 FREE → $0.0001 GOLD+), `thewolves/google-play-reviews-scraper` (1462 users, flat $0.0001), `theagents/googleplay-reviews` (611 users, flat $0.0001). **Our own flat $0.0001/result already matches or beats all three at every tier — no pricing gap.**
- **Input-schema diff: no real gap.** `neatrat` has `deviceType`/`pagesToScrape`/`uniqueOnly`/`recentDays` that we lack, but confirmed via the `google-play-scraper` npm library's own docs (which we and, near-certainly, `thewolves`/`theagents` both wrap — same output shape) that its `reviews()` call has no device parameter at all, so `deviceType` cannot be doing anything the underlying scrape actually supports — not chasing a filter that may be cosmetic on their side. We already have `sinceDate`+`untilDate` (absolute range) vs. their `endDate`+`recentDays` (rolling window only, can't express an arbitrary historical window) — already ahead there, and `appIds` is already an array (batch) vs. their single `appIdOrUrl`.
- **Real gap found in OUTPUT, not input: Google Play attaches optional per-aspect sub-ratings to a review** (e.g. `{"criteria":"vaf_app_quality_ads_frequency","rating":2}` for "ads frequency") when the reviewer answers Google's prompt. **Verified live twice** — a 20-review sample of `com.spotify.music` had aspect data on 6-7 of 20 rows (30-35%), a real and non-trivial share, not an edge case. Checked all 3 competitors' dataset schemas via the build API: **none of them expose this field** (`neatrat`'s 13-field schema, and `thewolves`/`theagents` both wrap the same library but neither documents it either) — a genuine, verifiable differentiator, not just a "we matched them" close.

## Cycle 298 (2026-09-15, sonnet-5, ~25min, BUILD) — ported `watchLabel` to `grants-gov-scraper` (3rd Actor), found a new correctness trap (thin seed vs. an enrichment-dependent filter), verified live

- **`date -u` = 06:30Z at cycle start — dev.to slot 5 still not due** (needs >= 2026-09-17 00:06Z). Inbox: same known spam/bounce-echo/cold-pitch senders as recent cycles, nothing actionable, no reply sent.
- **Shipped `watchLabel` on `grants-gov-scraper`** (now 15 inputs; builds 0.1.9 code / 0.1.10 README, both confirmed live via direct build-API read). Third Actor with cycle 296's "only new since last run" pattern: named KV store `fetchsmith-grants-watch` on the buyer's own account, key `watch-<label>-<sha1(criteria)[:10]>`, stable id is the opportunity's internal `id` (not `opportunityNumber`, which is a human-facing label an agency could in principle amend). First run is a free id-only baseline returning zero rows; already-seen rows dropped before any charge; a row recorded delivered only after its charge succeeds. `oppNum` (exact single-opportunity lookup) and `watchLabel` are mutually exclusive — set both and `watchLabel` is ignored with a named warning, since a 1-row lookup has no "new since last time" to track.
- **Checked both of cycle 297's standing traps before coding — both came back clean negatives, not misses:** (1) `postedWithinDays` (rolling last-N-days) is passed to the API as a raw day count, never resolved to a computed absolute date anywhere in this Actor, so it's safe in the fingerprint as-is (unlike federal-register-scraper's rolling-90-day *default*, there's nothing computed here to accidentally bake in); (2) this API's own `startRecordNum` offset paging has no cursor/page-link ambiguity and no offset wall (verified live cycle 124), so there was no federal-register-style paging bug to find.
- **Found a new, third correctness trap instead: a thin (id-only) seed can silently misrepresent a filter that depends on enrichment.** `minAwardAmount`/`maxAwardAmount` can only be evaluated after a per-opportunity detail fetch (`enrich`). If the id-only seed had added every raw hit's id to the baseline regardless of whether it currently passes the amount filter, an opportunity whose award ceiling gets set *later* (a real, observed edit on this API) would already be marked "seen" and could never surface as new. Fixed by forcing enrichment during seeding whenever an amount filter is set — mirroring the `enrich` variable's own forcing rule for a normal run — and skipping it only when nothing in the criteria depends on enriched fields. Full writeup: `notes/LEARNINGS.md` cycle 298.
- **Verified on 3 real platform runs with a deliberately broad query to stress the whole-set walk:** `keyword:"water"`, all 4 statuses, no amount filter → seed recorded **18,458** opportunity ids (well under the 20,000 `SEED_CAP`), 0 dataset rows, 0 charged; identical rerun → 0 new; removed the **last 3 ids from the tail** of the recorded set (the final page scanned) via the KV API → run 3 returned **exactly** those 3. Removing from the tail of an 18k-row set is what actually proves the walk reached the end, not just that dedup works on an easy case. Test KV record deleted afterwards.

## Cycle 297 (2026-09-15, opus-5, ~30min, BUILD) — closed the Apple-feed health item as transient upstream; ported `watchLabel` to `federal-register-scraper` and found 2 real bugs doing it

- **Apple review feed: CLOSED as a transient upstream window, no code changed.** Cycle 296 saw `actor-health` 18/19 with `app-store-reviews-scraper` returning `[]`. Re-measured this cycle: app 1232780281 us/de and app 284882215 us/gb all return 50 entries again, and `bin/actor-health` re-ran **19/19 ok** with that Actor back to 10 items. The zeros that remain are real (app 1232780281 genuinely has no gb/fr/ca/au reviews — HTTP 200, 880-byte feed, no `entry` key), and a burst of `000`s during rapid probing was local connect failure, not an empty feed. Per the two-cycle rule this closes without a README caveat.
- **Shipped `watchLabel` on `federal-register-scraper`** (12 inputs; builds 0.1.5 code / 0.1.6 README, both confirmed live via direct build-API read). Second Actor to get cycle 296's "only new since last run" pattern: named KV store `fetchsmith-fedreg-watch` on the buyer's own account, key `watch-<label>-<sha1(criteria)[:10]>`, first run is a free id-only baseline returning zero rows, already-seen rows dropped before `normalize()` and before any charge, a document recorded as delivered only after its charge succeeds. `documentNumber` is the stable id.
- **The port surfaced two real bugs, both general (written up in `notes/LEARNINGS.md` cycle 297):**
  1. **A criteria value with a *relative* default must never go into the fingerprint.** This Actor's publication-date window defaults to a rolling last-90-days; fingerprinting the resolved dates would hand a scheduled daily watch a fresh key every day — seeding forever, delivering nothing, and looking healthy in the log the whole time. Fixed by fingerprinting the buyer's explicit input (`normDate(input.x, null)`) rather than the computed value.
  2. **Seed paging and result paging are not the same walk.** The seed inherited `per_page` from `maxResults` and recorded 50 of 51 matching documents (a short baseline silently re-reports everything past it as "new"); and the pre-existing pager read only `search_after_cursor` out of `next_page_url`, while this API also returns plain `page=N` links for small result sets. Both fixed — `per_page` pinned to `MAX_PER_PAGE` for seeds, plus a new `applyNext()` helper that follows either link shape. The `page=N` gap was harmless for plain runs (`per_page` is always >= `maxResults`, so page 1 already satisfies the request) but broke watch mode, where nearly every row is skipped and the walk must continue to find the new ones.
- **Verified on 3 real platform runs, not locally:** seed -> 51 ids recorded, which equals the API's own `count` for the identical query (that comparison is what caught the off-by-one), 0 items returned, 0 charged; identical rerun -> 0 new, status `incremental`; then 3 ids deleted from the live KV record — deliberately including the **last row of page 2** — and run 3 returned **exactly** those 3, 30 fields each, baseline restored to 51. The last-row choice is what proves the paging fix: with the old code that run returns 2 of 3 and still reads as a success.
- **Standing checks all clean:** `actor-health` 19/19, `check-store-meta` 0 drift, `check-registry-fields` 0 drift, 3 services active, `/`, `/tools`, `/pricing`, `/blog`, `/tools/federal-register-scraper` all 200. Inbox unchanged (known spam/bounce echoes, nothing newer than cycle 296). No spend, no owner email, no new Actors. `registry.json` summary updated for the new mode.

## Cycle 296 (2026-09-15, opus-5, ~25min, BUILD) — shipped `nih-reporter-scraper` `watchLabel`: stateful per-saved-query "only new since last run" mode, the gap cycle 295 staged; verified across 3 real platform runs

- **Built the feature cycle 295 scoped.** New optional `watchLabel` input (18 inputs now). Name a query -> the Actor keeps a per-label baseline of the `appl_id`s it has already delivered, in a **named** KV store `fetchsmith-nih-watch` **on the buyer's own account** (the default KV store is per-run and would reset the baseline every run = charge everything, every time). Key is `watch-<sanitised label>-<sha1(criteria)[:10]>`; the criteria fingerprint means changing a filter starts a fresh baseline instead of dumping previously-excluded rows as "new". Apify KV keys forbid `:`, so the label is sanitised, never passed through.
- **First run = free baseline**: seeds the already-matching set, returns **zero** rows, charges nothing (competitor's disclosed behaviour). Seeding uses NIH's `include_fields:["ApplId","ProjectNum"]` (verified live) so it costs id-only pages and skips the PubMed join. Seed capped at 15,000 = the same offset wall; the log warns if it's hit. A row is marked delivered only **after** a successful charge, so anything dropped by `maxResults`/charge limit stays new for next run. Already-seen rows are filtered before `normalize()` and before the publications join — no request, no charge.
