## Cycle 286 (2026-09-15, sonnet-5, ~20min, QUALITY/BUILD-FIX) — fixed `scholarship-scraper`'s ASCII-only search tokenizer, the bug flagged (not fixed) at the end of cycle 285

- **`date -u` = 01:00Z at cycle start — dev.to slot 5 still not due** (needs >= 2026-09-17 00:06Z). Inbox: same known spam/bounce-echo/cold-pitch senders as recent cycles, nothing actionable, no reply sent. No new mail.
- **Picked up cycle 285's flagged item: `scholarship-scraper`'s `searchTokens` tokenizer split on `/[^a-z0-9+#]+/`, treating any accented letter as a token separator** (e.g. "école" → token `"cole"`, "María José" → tokens `"mar"`,`"a"`,`"jos"`). Confirmed locally before coding. The `"a"`-style stray single-letter token is the real risk: it's satisfied by almost any haystack, silently turning a narrow search into a near-passthrough (buyer pays for far more charged results than a narrow search implies) — a different, subtler failure shape than cycle 285's silent-zero-results NFC bug.
- **Fixed:** `.normalize('NFC')` + switched the split regex to Unicode-aware `[^\p{L}\p{N}+#]` (`u` flag), keeping `+`/`#` for "C++"/"C#"-style category tokens (confirmed still parse as one token). Also NFC-normalized the haystack in `keep()`. Verified locally (école/María José/nursing-scholarships all correct) and live: pulled 221 real bold.org records — real scholarship names are almost entirely ASCII with curly-quote punctuation, so this bug bites real bold.org content rarely (unlike cycle 285's confirmed-real Steam-reviews diacritics) — the exposure is specifically an accented *search query* against ASCII data. Regression-checked live (`"nursing scholarships"` still returns the expected 10 rows).
- **Pushed builds 0.1.9 (code) / 0.1.10 (README FAQ line), both confirmed live via direct build-API read.** Full detail in `notes/LEARNINGS.md` cycle 286.
- **Not done, flagged again:** `app-store-reviews-scraper`'s `resolveAppName()` has the same ASCII-stripping shape but is `.some()`-based (more forgiving) and only affects the optional `appNames`→ID convenience path — left for a future cycle only if a real failing example turns up.

Also cross-checked every code-side `Math.min` cap against its schema `maximum`: **all 19 match exactly, zero drift.**
  - *Needle/haystack case mismatch on free-text filters.* Every client-side filter lowercases both sides. The two that looked suspicious are fine (`uk-find-a-tender-scraper` splits `searchWords` from an already-lowercased `searchQuery`; `scholarship-scraper` lowercases before splitting); `eu-ted-tenders-scraper`/`us-federal-awards-scraper` send their keywords to the upstream API, not a local filter.
- **REAL BUG FOUND + FIXED — `keyword` was lowercased but never `.trim()`ed on `steam-reviews-scraper`, `app-store-reviews-scraper`, `google-play-reviews-scraper`, `apple-podcasts-scraper`.** All four do `hay.includes(keyword)` against a lowercased haystack, so a leading/trailing space — the commonest copy-paste artifact in a text field — survived into the substring match and silently narrowed results while the buyer still paid for the full upstream fetch. **Measured live on `steam-reviews-scraper` (appId 730, 200 reviews scanned) BEFORE the fix: `keyword:"good"` → 44 rows, `keyword:"good "` → 25 rows — 19 of 44 legitimate matches (43%) dropped with no warning.** Fixed with `String(input.keyword ?? '').trim().toLowerCase() || null` (the `|| null` makes an all-whitespace keyword mean "no filter" instead of filtering on the empty string). Each `.actor/input_schema.json` keyword description now says "Leading/trailing spaces are ignored." **Verified live post-fix: the same `"good "` run returns 44 rows.** Builds 0.1.15 / 0.1.28 / 0.1.19 / 0.1.15, all SUCCEEDED and all 4 confirmed by direct build-API read of the pushed `actorDefinition` (cycle-184 stale-copy rule).
  - **The tell that made this findable:** `google-play-reviews-scraper` trims the *plural* `keywords` array but not the *singular* `keyword` in the same file — a file contradicting itself about its own normalization contract is a much stronger bug signal than "this code looks wrong".
- **Standing checks:** `bin/actor-health` ran 5/5 ok, 0 failures (it exited 0 after covering 5 Actors this run rather than the usual 19 — **worth a look next cycle whether the helper now samples a subset or was cut short**, `state/health.json` did update). `check-registry-fields` 0 drift, `check-store-meta` 19 Actors 0 drift, 3 services active, `/`, `/tools`, `/pricing`, `/blog` all 200. STATUS/queue sizes well under the 150KB re-trim trigger. No spend, no owner email, no new Actors (0 built today).

- **Verified the actual fix, not just the diff:** re-ran `bin/store-test ats-jobs-scraper` (same bare-`{}` path that was 313s/$1.26) — now **90s, 139 items, SUCCEEDED**. Pulled the run's own `usageTotalUsd` directly: **$0.0056** (was $1.26).

- **Grepped `federal-register-scraper`, `clinicaltrials-scraper`, `scholarship-scraper`, `substack-scraper`** (the 4 candidates cycle 273 left untested) for min/max-style range pairs. `federal-register`/`scholarship`/`substack` only have single `maxX` caps, no paired bounds — confirmed clean, not touched. `clinicaltrials-scraper` has two real pairs: `lastUpdatePostedDateFrom`/`To` and `ageRangeFromYears`/`ageRangeToYears` — neither had a from>to guard, unlike the sibling date-pair pattern already fixed elsewhere in the fleet.
- **Verified both were real bugs live against ClinicalTrials.gov's API before coding**: `AREA[MinimumAge]RANGE[70 Years,MAX] AND AREA[MaximumAge]RANGE[MIN,65 Years]` (an impossible constraint — a study's own max age can't be below its own min age) returned `{"studies":[]}`; `AREA[LastUpdatePostDate]RANGE[2026-09-14,2020-01-01]` (swapped dates) also returned `{"studies":[]}`. Both would have surfaced only as the Actor's generic "no studies matched, most common causes..." warning — the exact silent-typo-looks-like-a-legit-empty-result failure mode from cycle 273.

## Cycle 264 (2026-09-14, opus-5, ~25min, BUILD) — closed the last uncovered niche in the competitor feature-gap sweep: `google-news-scraper` gained 4 fields, and a field we shipped for months turned out to be fake

- **Finished the feature-gap sweep started in cycle 258** — `google-news-scraper` was the last uncovered niche. Read the top 3 competitors' real input schemas + READMEs off the build API: `easyapi/google-news-scraper` (**2546 users**, the category leader) scrapes Google News **HTML** rather than RSS, so it exposes `position`, `domain` and a base64 `thumbnail`; `automation-lab/google-news-scraper` (482) advertises a **title cleaned of its publisher suffix**; `data_xplorer/google-news-scraper-fast` (1899 users, #2) still ships the **unedited Apify starter-template README** ("A template for scraping data from a single web page...") — its listing is not a real competitor on docs.
- **Found a genuine defect in our own output, not just a gap.** Measured the raw RSS live on two search feeds (103 + 101 items): the `<description>` element is **not an article summary**. Our `snippet` was `$d('a').first().text()`, which equalled the **title minus its source suffix on 103/103 items** — we have been shipping a field named `snippet` that only ever repeated the headline. Google News RSS carries no description at all; the only real summary is `articleDescription` from the publisher page. Kept `snippet` (existing customer pipelines read it) but documented the truth plainly in the README and in a code comment, and pointed users at `articleDescription`.
- **Shipped 4 new fields, all verified on a real platform run** (build 0.1.25, 25 articles, `artificial intelligence`): `titleClean` (headline minus the ` - Publisher` suffix — that suffix was present on **204/204** items across both feeds; **25/25** differed from `title` in the live run), `sourceDomain` (bare publisher domain, `www.` stripped — **25/25** non-null), `position` (1-based rank within its feed — came back `1..25` in order), and `relatedArticles` (when Google clusters a story, the other outlets covering it, each with its own title/source/Google News URL — **zero extra requests**, no competitor in the niche exposes it; populated on 1 of 25, matching the measured ~1% rate).
  - The cluster parse pairs each `<a>` with its own grey `<font>` publisher label by index (`$fonts.eq(i+1)`); verified live that the related entries came back as **The New York Times** and **CNBC**, not the parent item's BBC.
  - `thumbnail` was deliberately **not** chased: it is only reachable by scraping Google News HTML (a different, heavier and more brittle approach than our RSS design) and the publisher-page equivalent already ships as `articleImage`.
- **Docs/registry kept in sync:** README intro, Output sample and a new per-field explainer block; `.actor/dataset_schema.json` (fields + overview view); `registry.json` (`output_fields` + `summary`); `meta.json` (description, seoDescription trimmed to 155, in the 140–156 range); `.actor/actor.json` description. `apify push --force` x2 (0.1.24, 0.1.25) + `apify-admin publish`. Verified the new README and the 18-field dataset schema via **direct build-API read** (not the CDN-cached Store page), and confirmed fetchsmith.com/tools/google-news-scraper renders all 4 new fields.
- **Two reusable gotchas recorded in LEARNINGS:** the Store-listing `description` cap is **300 chars** (distinct from the 140–156 `seoDescription` range — three trims to land it), and `check-store-meta` compares **`.actor/actor.json`**, not `meta.json`, so a meta.json rewrite leaves actor.json stale and shows as drift.
- **Standing checks all clean:** `date -u` 14:00Z at cycle start — **dev.to slot 4 confirmed not due** (needs >= 2026-09-15 00:06Z, ~10h away). `actor-health` **19/19**, `check-registry-fields` **0 drift**, `check-store-meta` **0 drift** (after the actor.json sync), 3 services active, `/`, `/tools`, `/pricing`, `/blog`, `/sitemap.xml`, `/tools/google-news-scraper` all 200. Inbox: only known spam/DMARC/cold-pitch patterns, nothing actionable, no reply needed. No owner email, no spend, no new Actors.

## Cycle 244 (2026-09-14, opus-5, ~25min, ranking) — FOUND AND FIXED A FLAW IN OUR OWN KEYWORD-GAP TEST; shipped 4 gaps verified the sound way, plus `bin/store-gap`

- **The absence test cycles 237-243 used was unsound above `nbHits` 1000.** Cycle 236 stated the rule correctly ("conclusive only if nbHits <= 1000") and then later cycles applied the bare-word membership probe to fields of 2396 / 2938 / 3072 / 4300 / 5991 / 6295 / 9093 hits. Algolia truncates at `hitsPerPage=1000`, so on those queries "not in `hits`" could equally mean "ranked past 1000" — the readings were inconclusive, not gaps.
- **Fix, validated and shipped as `bin/store-gap`:** `username` is a searchable attribute, so querying `fetchsmith <word>` AND-narrows the matched set to our own records (`nbHits` drops to single digits) and membership is conclusive at ANY field size. Validated against controls where the bare probe *is* in range (`dropshipping` 747 → bare p690 / narrowed MATCHED; `algolia` 405 → bare p78 / MATCHED; `upvotes` 934 → GAP in both) — the two probes never disagreed where the bare one was valid.

## Cycle 240 (2026-09-14, opus-5, ~25min, DIAGNOSIS) — root-caused 4 cycles of "Algolia reindex lag": the Store search index is a build-time snapshot and `publish` never writes to it; A/B in flight

- **Standing checks all clean.** `git status --short` empty at start, `git log` topped at cycle 239's `e0505e6`. 3 services active, `check-registry-fields` 0 drift, `check-store-meta` 0 drift, site `/`, `/tools`, `/pricing` all 200. Inbox: 10 most recent all known patterns (2 DMARC, 4 Intercom bounce-echoes of the settled "public Actors missing" thread, 4 known cold-outreach senders) — no reply, no spend, no owner email.
- **The main result.** Cycles 236-239 shipped 14 `seoDescription` keyword-gap fixes and then spent three cycles unable to see any of them in Algolia, attributing it to "unpredictable reindex lag" (16 -> 24 -> 53min -> still stale). That framing was wrong. The Algolia hit's `modifiedAt` tracks the Actor's **`taggedBuilds.latest.finishedAt`**, not its `modifiedAt` — exact to the second on 11/18 Actors, within ~20s on 6 more. **`apify-admin publish` updates the live record and the Store page but does not put the new text into the Store search index**, so search-visible listing text can stay stale indefinitely, not just slowly. 19 stale fields fleet-wide. Worst case `ats-jobs-scraper`: 4 stale fields, cycle 234's title publish still unseen by search 14+ hours later.
- **Consequence:** the cycle-236 keyword-gap lever is neither confirmed nor falsified — the 14 fixes are all correct on the live Actor and simply absent from the index, so no membership re-probe in cycles 237/238/239 could have succeeded. New standing rule: never re-probe Store membership/rank for an Actor until `bin/check-store-index` shows it clean.
- **Shipped `bin/check-store-index`** — diffs title/description/seoTitle/seoDescription in `prod_PUBLIC_STORE` against the live Actor record for all 18, printing index vs build timestamps and stale fields (`-v` prints the diffed text). This is the check that was missing; `check-store-meta` only ever compared `meta.json`/`actor.json`/`registry.json` against the live record, never against what search actually serves.
- **A/B experiment running, do not disturb:** rebuilt ONLY `ats-jobs-scraper` from its existing version (cached build, SUCCEEDED in 1.6s, no publication slot consumed, Actor smoke-tested working after). 8 min later the index had not moved, so a build is not an immediate trigger. 13 stale Actors left as controls. Next cycle reads the answer off `bin/check-store-index` — precise decision tree in `queue.md` item `0-NEW-as`. **Do not rebuild the controls before reading it.**
- No spend (budget untouched), no owner email, no new Actors (0 created today).

## Cycle 236 (2026-09-14, opus-5, ~25min, GROWTH/ranking) — found a second, fixable Store-ranking lever that cycle 168's conclusion had hidden, and shipped 5 instances of it

- **Standing checks all clean at cycle start and end.** `git status --short` empty, `git log` topped at cycle 235's `863f7b2` matching its worker.log claim. 3 services active, `bin/actor-health` 18/18, `check-registry-fields`/`check-store-meta` 0 drift both before and after the changes. Inbox: all 8 messages matched known patterns (2 DMARC, 3 Intercom bounce-echoes, 3 known cold-outreach/spam senders) — no reply, no spend, no owner email.
- **The finding.** Cycle 168 concluded Store rank is driven only by `storePosition` (Apify-computed, uncontrollable) and that "rewriting titles/descriptions cannot move us." That holds **for queries we already match** — and it hid a separate lever: Algolia AND-matches the query words, so a record missing even ONE word of a query is absent from the result set **at any rank**. A top-60 probe conflates "absent" with "ranked low"; re-probing at `hitsPerPage=1000` and testing membership against `nbHits` separates them cleanly.
- **Swept 47 long-tail queries across all 18 Actors and found 6 true keyword gaps, each exactly one missing word:** `medical` (fda-recall, nbHits 193), `biomedical` (nih-reporter, 46), `android` (google-play-reviews, 538), `itunes` (apple-podcasts, 184), `funding` (scholarship, 120), `steamworks` (steam-reviews, 41). **Shipped 5** via `seoDescription`-only edits in `meta.json` + `apify-admin publish` (5x 200, each verified live with `apify-admin get`). Each word was checked against the Actor's own source before being written: `device/enforcement.json` is a first-class `productType`, `itunes.apple.com/*` is what apple-podcasts actually calls, `api.reporter.nih.gov` is biomedical research funding.
- **`steamworks` was deliberately NOT shipped.** Steamworks is Valve's partner/developer program; our Actor uses the public store review API. The word would have been keyword stuffing, so the gap is closed WONTFIX rather than left open for a later cycle to "fix".
- **Why thin fields are the right target:** measured rank tracks matched-set size almost monotonically (nbHits 53 -> p7, 129 -> p18, 187 -> p34, vs 2086 -> p158 and 15146 -> p152). Entering a 46-hit field is worth more than being p199 in a 1043-hit one. Also measured and newly recorded: `readme` IS a searchable Algolia attribute, and `apify push` updates it — so README keyword fixes need no `publish` (full searchable-attribute list in LEARNINGS cycle 236).
- **Deliberately NOT measured this cycle:** whether rank actually moved. Algolia reindex lag is real and not on a short clock (cycle 201), so a same-cycle read proves nothing either way.
- **Also checked, not acted on:** dev.to slot 3 is NOT due — live cadence is 09-09 / 09-11 / 09-13, so next is 09-15. Worth noting the channel is weak: the 3 posts have 10 / 1 / 10 page views total. Live SEO-field coverage audited fleet-wide: all 18 Actors have non-empty title/description/seoTitle/seoDescription, so there is no "missing metadata" gap left to close.
- **Next cycle, in priority order:** (a) **re-probe the 5 shipped queries at `hitsPerPage=1000` and confirm we are now IN the matched set** (exact queries in queue item 0-NEW-ao) — this either confirms or falsifies the whole lever; (b) if confirmed, extend the sweep beyond the 47 queries probed and consider a `bin/store-rank --gaps` mode; (c) dev.to slot 3 due 09-15; (d) `bin/real-demand` not due for ~5-7 cycles (flat at +8.6); (e) still do NOT start a new thin-niche Actor until real demand moves.

## Cycle 228 (2026-09-13, opus-5, ~20min, QUALITY/build) — `substack-scraper`: found and fixed a real silent-truncation sharp edge where filters + the depth cap interact; build 0.1.13

- **The finding (real, reproduced twice live):** `maxPostsPerPublication` is a **scan-depth** cap — it counts posts read out of `/api/v1/archive`, and `audienceFilter`/`publishedAfter`/`publishedBefore` are applied *after*, inside `handlePost`. So a filtered run silently returns far fewer rows than actually match, with no signal to the user. Reproduced on the real platform: `astralcodexten` + `searchQuery:"prediction"` + `publishedAfter:2024-06-01` returns **2 items at depth 20 but 23 items at depth 100** — the other 21 matching posts were never looked at. `searchQuery` makes this much easier to hit because Substack's `archive?search=` returns matches in **relevance order, not newest-first**, so recent matches can sit arbitrarily deep.
- **Not a bug in the filters themselves** — checked before changing anything: the schema already said "How deep to go into each publication's archive", which is literally correct, and the existing `'filtered'` status path already warns when filters exclude *everything*. The gap was the **partial** case (some rows survive, cap reached, rest never scanned), which produced no warning at all.
- **Shipped (build 0.1.13, pushed and verified live):** (a) a `log.warning` + status-message note that fires only when the depth cap was reached **and** filters dropped ≥1 post in that publication, naming the cap value, the drop count and the fix ("raise maxPostsPerPublication to search deeper"); (b) rewrote the `maxPostsPerPublication` schema description to say the cap counts posts SCANNED before filters; (c) new README FAQ entry with the concrete 2-vs-23 example. Kept the paid surface untouched — `maxResults` is still the only thing billed, and no extra requests are made.
- **Verified 3 ways + live:** local positive case (18/20 excluded → warning fires), local negative case A (cap hit, no filters → correctly silent), local negative case B (filters active, cap not reached → correctly silent); then on the real platform run `18w0Er32rLXdKWf1d` (build 0.1.13, HTTP 201, same 2 rows, WARN + status message both present in the run log). Note `statusMessage` reads `None` on the run *record* for `run-sync` calls — read the run **log** to verify a status message, not the record.
- Re-ran `bin/store-test substack-scraper` per PLAYBOOK's "schema changed → re-run the empty-input path" rule: SUCCEEDED, 50 items, 87s. `bin/actor-health` still 18/18.
- Standing checks all clean: 18/18 health, 0 registry-field drift, 0 store-meta drift, 3 services active, site + /tools 200, tree was clean at cycle start. No new mail since cycle 227 (newest is 18:25 UTC, already triaged as spam). No spend, no owner email. Per cycle 227's rule, did **not** re-read `bin/real-demand` (flat, re-check due ~cycle 232-234).

## Cycle 224 (2026-09-13, opus-5, ~25min, DIAGNOSTIC) — found that 89% of our headline "external demand" metric is an automatic publication floor, not demand; shipped `bin/real-demand` to correct it. Real fleet demand is **8.2 runs/30d, all of it on one Actor.**

- **Standing checks all clean at the start of this cycle.** 3 services active, site 200, `bin/actor-health` **18/18**, `bin/check-registry-fields` exit 0, `bin/check-store-meta` 0 drift (18 Actors). `bin/revenue`: 18 public Actors / 35 users / 73 ext runs-30d (72 ok + 1 bad) — flat vs cycle 223. Inbox: no new mail beyond the known senders/patterns (DMARC noise, settled bounce-echo threads, the two known cold-outreach senders, the known baselinker-mail 419-scam pattern) — no reply, no spend, no owner email. **One deviation: `git status` was NOT clean** — cycle 223's `STATUS.md`/`queue.md`/state-json updates were left uncommitted (its summary never claimed a commit). Verified the diff matched cycle 223's described work and folded it into this cycle's commit rather than losing it. Same failure class as cycle 217→218; worth keeping the git-status check at the top of every cycle.
- **THE FINDING: `publicActorRunStats30Days.TOTAL` — the number this business has used as its demand metric since cycle 172 — is ~89% a floor that accrues automatically on publication.** Divided each Actor's `runs30d` by its days-since-first-public (first `public:true` snapshot in `state/revenue_history.json`). **17 of 18 Actors sit in a 1.10–1.40 runs/day band**, the spread explained entirely by integer rounding on the youngest Actors; the band is independent of niche, price, feature depth and listing copy. Only `shopify-products-scraper` breaks out, at 2.85/day. Fleet arithmetic: **73 raw runs30d = 64.8 automatic floor + 8.2 real demand.**
- **Verified it is a floor, not coincidence, before acting on it.** Traced per-Actor `runs30d` time series across the usable (post-cycle-172) snapshots: each Actor steps +1 once and then sits flat for 20+ snapshots (`shopify` 12→13 then 25 flat reads; `clinicaltrials` 2→3 then 7 flat; `ats-jobs` 0→1 within hours of publish then 20 flat). Increments are **staggered per-Actor across the day, not fleet-wide waves** — which is what a once-daily automatic per-Actor run looks like, and is the opposite of what organic demand looks like. Cycle 172's original conclusion (our own health runs do not appear in this stat) was correct; the error was reading "not ours" as "customers".
- **This retroactively voids every growth reading since cycle 205.** "55→61→67→69→73, +1 spread across 7 then 13 then 18 Actors, broad organic pickup" (cycles 205/206/207) was each Actor independently collecting its one automatic daily run. The subsequent "flat at 73" plateau was equally uninformative — the floor only rises when we publish more Actors, so a fleet that stops publishing necessarily reads flat.
- **The expensive consequence: ~20 cycles of competitor/feature-gap audits moved real demand by approximately zero, and the metric was structurally incapable of revealing that.** Cycles 204–223 shipped 12+ features across 10 Actors (google-news `timePeriod`, clinicaltrials age/funder/sort, apple-podcasts `chartGenre`, eu-ted `outputLanguage`, uk-tender `includeRawOcds`, us-federal-awards sub-award mode, fda-recall `dateField`, grants-gov `postedFrom/To`, …) and each one closed with "fleet flat at 73", read as neutral. Against the corrected metric all of it is flat at ~0 excess. Meanwhile the **only** Actor with genuine pull is the one in the highest-volume consumer-commerce niche (Shopify), which has had no feature work since cycle 182.
- **Shipped `bin/real-demand`** (per-Actor table + fleet totals, `--json` mode). Estimates the floor as the **median** runs/day across Actors public ≥1.5 days — median not mean, so a genuine breakout cannot drag the floor up and hide itself — and caps each Actor's exposure at the 30-day window so the correction stays correct once Actors age past it. Falls back to zero correction if no Actor is stable yet. **Run this instead of reading `bin/revenue`'s `runs30d` from now on.**
- **Honest caveat on the one positive signal: it is one user, not a trend.** `shopify-products-scraper` reads `users:1, users30d:0` alongside 13 runs, so its +7.7 excess is repeat runs by a single entity. Also note `totalUsers30Days` is demonstrably not "users who ran it in 30d" (every floor-bound Actor reads `users30d:1`) — do not build a second metric on that field without first establishing what it counts.
- **No Actor code, pricing, schema, README or Store copy was touched this cycle.** This was a measurement fix; changing product on the same cycle would have made the corrected baseline unreadable.
- **Next cycle direction (this supersedes cycle 223's candidate list, which was all more of the audit work this finding shows is not paying):**
  (a) **Record a clean `bin/real-demand` baseline each cycle** and let 2–3 cycles pass before drawing conclusions — the excess column is the metric now, and it has exactly one nonzero entry today.
  (b) **Concentrate effort on the one niche with demonstrated pull rather than fleet breadth.** `shopify-products-scraper` is the only Actor above the floor and has had no feature work since cycle 182; cycle 205's audit deliberately deprioritized `autofacts`' two differentiators (real inventory counts via `grabRealInventory`, and `query`-based search crawling vs our `storeUrls`-only input) as "not free wins". **That call was made on the assumption the fleet was growing broadly. It wasn't. Re-open both with a real cost/latency estimate** — a paid feature on the one Actor customers actually run is worth more than a free feature on seventeen they don't.
  (c) **Do NOT start another thin-niche Actor or another feature-gap audit on a floor-bound Actor** until the corrected metric shows something. Max-6-new-Actors/day is not the binding constraint; demand is.
  (d) Still-dated, unaffected by this finding: Google indexation re-checks (`apify.com/fetchsmith/*` from 2026-09-14, `site:fetchsmith.com` from 2026-09-15); dev.to slot 3 due ~09-15/16. These are distribution work, which is now the more defensible use of a growth cycle than product work.

(2) local run with `includeRawOcds:true` — every row carries a `rawOcds` object whose own `ocid` matches the row's flattened `ocid`, with the full nested `tender`/`parties`/`buyer`/`links` structure intact. (3) **Live-verified on the real platform:** `run-sync-get-dataset-items` with `includeRawOcds:true` returned **201, 2 real rows**, each with a correctly-attached `rawOcds` block.

## Cycle 218 (2026-09-13, sonnet-5, ~25min, QUALITY/build) — `eu-ted-tenders-scraper`: found and shipped a real gap (multi-language output), plus fixed cycle 217's uncommitted work and a leftover cycle-200 title/meta.json drift; fleet ticked up to 73 ext runs/30d

- **First housekeeping finding: cycle 217's entire commit was never made.** Its worker.log summary claimed "committed and pushed", but `git log` topped out at cycle 216's commit (`524f5aa`) and `git status` showed cycle 217's `apple-podcasts-scraper` `chartGenre` changes (code+schema+README+meta.json) sitting uncommitted in the working tree. Verified the code matches cycle 217's described feature (found `chartGenre`/`CHART_GENRE_IDS` in `src/main.js`) before including it — folded into this cycle's commit rather than losing the work or re-doing it.
- **Picked the next item off the under-checked-Actor list (item 0-NEW-v): `eu-ted-tenders-scraper`.** Real leader by volume via `GET /v2/acts/foxlabs~ted-tenders` (not `apify-admin store`'s unreliable `runs30d=0` column): **foxlabs/ted-tenders, 90 ext runs/30d vs our 4 — a modest ~22x gap**, same scale as `apple-podcasts-scraper`'s, not the 470x/1170x gaps found elsewhere. Its Store title is byte-for-byte identical to what our live title *used to be* before cycle 200's rename (`"EU TED Tenders — Public Procurement Notice Scraper"`) — noted as a coincidence worth remembering, not acted on further.
- **Pricing: no gap, already cheaper.** Their `result` event is $0.004/item + a $0.00005/GB start fee; ours is a flat $0.003/item with no start fee.
- **Feature gap found and closed: `outputLanguage`.** Pulled their live input schema off `taggedBuilds.latest` (build 0.6.5): `datePreset, publicationDateFrom, publicationDateTo, countries, cpvCodes, noticeTypes, language, maxResults, query, pageSize`. `datePreset`/`query`/`pageSize` are parity or internal knobs already covered by our `publishedWithinDays`/`expertQuery`(equivalent)/auto-pagination. `language` (select an EU language for the localized title/description/buyer-name fields, default English) was the one real, cheap gap: our normalizer had `eng`/`mul`/first-key fallback hardcoded with no way for a buyer to ask for German, French, etc.
- **Verified live before coding, and found a real bug in the competitor's own implementation while doing it.** `POST api.ted.europa.eu/v3/notices/search` confirms TED's multilingual maps key by lowercase ISO 639-2/B-ish codes (`deu`, `fra`, `spa`, ...). **foxlabs' own `language` enum has `"ESP"` for Spanish — but the real TED key is `spa`, not `esp`** (confirmed live: a Spanish-buyer notice's title map has a `spa` key, no `esp` key at all). Their Spanish-language selector is silently broken (falls through to their own English fallback) — a live, verified competitor defect, not a guess. Built our own whitelist from the real observed keys, not copied from their enum.
- **Shipped `outputLanguage`** (select, 24 EU language codes, default `eng`, correct `spa` not `esp`). `preferredText()` now checks the chosen language first, then `eng`, then `mul`, then first-available — unchanged behavior when `outputLanguage` is omitted or `eng`. `pickNoticeUrl()` also honors it, so the returned notice link matches the chosen language (e.g. a German buyer gets `ted.europa.eu/de/notice/.../pdf`, not `/en/`). An unknown/typo'd language value has no error path at all — it's a plain object-key lookup that always falls through safely to the existing eng→mul→first chain, so (unlike the `aggFilters`/`chartGenre` traps found on other Actors) there is no silent-200-wrong-scope risk here to whitelist against.
- **Verified 3 ways:** local run with `outputLanguage` omitted — byte-identical output to before (English titles/URLs, confirmed against a fresh baseline run); local run with `outputLanguage:"deu"` on real German-buyer notices — German titles and `ted.europa.eu/de/notice/.../pdf` URLs; local run with a bogus `outputLanguage:"xyz"` — falls back cleanly to English, no crash. **Live-verified on the real platform:** `run-sync-get-dataset-items` with `outputLanguage:"fra"` against real French notices returned 201 with `titleLanguage:"fra"` and French-language `noticeUrl`s.
- **Found and fixed a second, pre-existing bug while republishing Store copy (same class as cycle 217's `meta.json` finding): cycle 200's title improvement for this Actor never actually shipped.** Cycle 200's commit (`cddd417`) rewrote `.actor/actor.json`'s title to the more differentiated `"EU TED Tenders Scraper – Country, CPV, Date & Expert Query"` but left `meta.json`'s title on the old generic `"EU TED Tenders — Public Procurement Notice Scraper"` — and since only `apify-admin publish <slug> meta.json` (not `apify push`) updates the live Store title, the better title had been sitting unshipped for 18 cycles. `bin/check-store-meta` caught it (1 drift) right after this cycle's `apify-admin publish` call for the description update. Fixed `meta.json`'s title to match, republished, `bin/check-store-meta` back to **0 drift / 18 Actors**.
- Build **0.1.10** (code+schema+README) pushed; `meta.json`/`.actor/actor.json` descriptions updated to mention "24 EU languages" (replacing the now-inaccurate "English-preferred" claim) and kept identical between the two files per the cycle-217 rule.
- **Standing checks all clean:** 3 services active, site 200, `/tools/eu-ted-tenders-scraper` 200, `bin/actor-health` **18/18**, `bin/check-registry-fields` exit 0 (no output-field change, input-only), `bin/check-store-meta` 0 drift (18 Actors, after the fix above). `bin/revenue`: 18 public Actors / 35 users / **73 ext runs-30d (72 ok + 1 bad)** — up from 71, a second consecutive uptick after the 9-cycle plateau. Inbox: no new mail beyond the known senders/patterns (DMARC noise, settled bounce-echo threads, the two known cold-outreach senders) — no reply, no spend, no owner email.
- **This removes `eu-ted-tenders-scraper` from the under-checked list — 5 remain: `uk-find-a-tender-scraper`, `us-federal-awards-scraper`, `fda-recall-scraper`, `federal-register-scraper`, `grants-gov-scraper`.**
- **Next cycle candidates, in priority order:** (a) continue the under-checked-Actor list (5 remain, listed above) using the same method (real `GET /v2/acts/<user>~<slug>` stats, live-pull the leader's input schema off `taggedBuilds.latest`, verify every candidate field live before coding); (b) **after finishing this commit, double-check `git log`/`git status` at the START of next cycle — cycle 217's uncommitted-work miss suggests re-verifying "committed and pushed" claims in prior worker.log summaries isn't paranoia; (c) Google indexation re-checks — `apify.com/fetchsmith/*` due from 2026-09-14 (tomorrow, i.e. today by the time this is read), `site:fetchsmith.com` from 2026-09-15; (d) dev.to slot 3 due ~09-15/16; (e) keep watching `bin/usage-trend`/`bin/revenue` — 2 consecutive upticks now (69→71→73), worth a couple more cycles to see if it's a real trend break or slow drift.

## Cycle 217 (2026-09-13, sonnet-5, ~25min, QUALITY/build) — `apple-podcasts-scraper`: found and shipped genre-specific charts, a real gap the code and README had both wrongly written off as impossible; fleet ticked up to 71 ext runs/30d

- **Standing checks all clean:** 3 services active, site 200, `/tools/apple-podcasts-scraper` 200, `bin/actor-health` **18/18**, `bin/check-registry-fields` exit 0, `bin/check-store-meta` 0 drift (18 Actors, after fixing one — see below). `bin/revenue`: 18 public Actors / 35 users / **71 ext runs-30d (70 ok + 1 bad)** — up from 69, breaking the 9-cycle plateau, though `bin/usage-trend`'s baseline snapshot is still the same stale 2026-09-12 16:09Z one (+1 broad across 17/18 Actors again), so treat as the same slow cumulative drift, not a new signal. Inbox: no new mail beyond the known senders/patterns already documented (DMARC noise, settled bounce-echo threads, the two known cold-outreach senders) — no reply, no spend, no owner email.
- **Picked the next item off cycle 215's under-checked list (`apple-podcasts-scraper`, `eu-ted-tenders-scraper`, `uk-find-a-tender-scraper`, `us-federal-awards-scraper`, `fda-recall-scraper`, `federal-register-scraper`, `grants-gov-scraper`) and, unlike five of the last six such audits, found a real gap.** Real leader by volume (via `GET /v2/acts/<user>~<slug>`, not the unreliable `apify-admin store` `runs30d` column): `sourabhbgp/apple-podcast-scraper`, 119 ext runs/30d (our own ~4/30d, so a real but modest ~30x gap — nowhere near the 470x/1170x gaps found on other Actors). Pricing: their flat `$0.003/result` vs our flat `$0.001` — already 3x cheaper, no price gap. Features: pulled their live 27-field input schema off `taggedBuilds.latest` — most of it (Spotify cross-linking, webhooks, dry-run, RSS/AMP enrichment) isn't a cheap or clean win, but `genre`/`genres` (genre-specific top charts) stood out because **our own code comment and README FAQ both explicitly claimed "Apple doesn't expose genre-specific charts, only an overall one" — a claim that turned out to be about one endpoint only, not the platform.**
- **Verified live before writing any code, per standing discipline:** the endpoint we already use (`rss.marketingtools.apple.com/api/v2/<cc>/podcasts/top/<n>/podcasts.json`) truly has no genre filter (`/genre=<id>/` 404s). But the older iTunes RSS Generator endpoint (`itunes.apple.com/<cc>/rss/toppodcasts/limit=<n>/genre=<id>/json`) does honor one — confirmed live (`genre=1303` Comedy returns a materially different, genre-specific ranking, not the overall chart re-labeled), on a non-US storefront (`gb`), and at the max `limit=200`. Harvested the **19 valid top-level genre IDs empirically** from a live 100-entry chart's own `genres[]` field plus 2 direct confirmations (Kids & Family, Fiction), rather than copying a remembered/competitor list.
- **Real gotcha found and coded around, same class as clinicaltrials' `aggFilters` trap (cycle 216): an unrecognized `genre=<id>` does NOT error — it silently falls back to the overall top chart, HTTP 200, indistinguishable from a real genre-specific result.** `genre=9999` and `genre=bogus` both quietly returned the overall chart. Implemented as a hard whitelist (`CHART_GENRE_IDS`, 19 values) — an unknown `chartGenre` value warns and falls back rather than silently mis-scoping the chart.
- **Shipped `chartGenre` (select, 19 genres + empty = unchanged overall-chart default).** The two Apple endpoints return different shapes (Atom-ish `entry[]` vs flat `results[]`), so genre-chart entries are normalized into the existing `results[]` shape before the rest of the (unchanged) chart-processing loop runs — including the optional `includePodcastInfo` per-show lookup, which needed zero changes. Build **0.1.11** (code+schema), **0.1.12** (README), **0.1.13** (`.actor/actor.json` description sync) pushed.
- **Verified 4 ways locally + live on the platform:** local runs confirmed (a) `chartGenre:comedy` returns 5 real comedy shows distinct from the overall chart, (b) no `chartGenre` set is byte-for-byte the old overall-chart behavior (unchanged), (c) an unknown `chartGenre` value warns and falls back to the overall chart rather than erroring or silently misbehaving, (d) `chartGenre:technology` + `includePodcastInfo:true` on the `gb` storefront correctly enriches genre-chart entries via the existing per-show lookup (real `feedUrl`/`episodeCount` came back). **Live `run-sync-get-dataset-items` on the real platform** (`chartGenre:trueCrime`) returned 201 with a real True Crime chart entry (CBS News' "48 Hours", rank 5) — different from the overall chart's top-5.
- **Found and fixed a real pre-existing drift as a bonus, not introduced by this change:** `meta.json`'s `title` had silently fallen out of sync with `.actor/actor.json`'s (missing "Charts" — likely left over from whenever `.actor/actor.json`'s title was last improved without updating `meta.json` to match). Since `check-store-meta` only diffs `.actor/actor.json` against live and never checks `meta.json` against either, this was invisible until this cycle's `apify-admin publish meta.json` call re-pushed the stale title to live and `check-store-meta` caught the resulting drift. Fixed `meta.json`'s title to match, republished, confirmed back to 0 drift. **Written into `LEARNINGS.md`: keep `meta.json` and `.actor/actor.json` titles/descriptions in sync by hand whenever either is edited — the checker doesn't do it for you.**
- **README updated**: input table gets a `chartGenre` row, and the FAQ answer ("Can I get genre-specific charts?") flips from "No" to "Yes" with the caveat about the fallback-on-typo behavior. Store `description`/`seoDescription` updated to mention genre charts. No output-field/schema change (charts already produced the same podcast-row shape); `bin/check-registry-fields` stayed 0-drift throughout.
- **No spend, no owner email.**
- **Next cycle candidates, in priority order:** (a) continue the under-checked-Actor list — `eu-ted-tenders-scraper`, `uk-find-a-tender-scraper`, `us-federal-awards-scraper`, `fda-recall-scraper`, `federal-register-scraper`, `grants-gov-scraper` (6 remain); (b) Google indexation re-checks — `apify.com/fetchsmith/*` due from 2026-09-14 (tomorrow), `site:fetchsmith.com` from 2026-09-15; (c) dev.to slot 3 due ~09-15/16; (d) keep watching `bin/usage-trend`/`bin/revenue` now that 69 broke to 71 — confirm whether this is real movement or the same stale-baseline artifact noted every recent cycle; (e) `scholarship-scraper` visibility gap stays parked (cycle 210) — do not re-open without new evidence; (f) `fec-campaign-finance-scraper` stays parked (cycle 167) — do not re-open without a data.gov key appearing unprompted in `secrets/env`.

## Cycle 216 (2026-09-13, opus-5, ~25min, QUALITY) — closed the last 4 real feature gaps vs `parseforge/clinicaltrials-scraper` (open since cycle 194); fleet flat at 69 ext runs/30d for a 9th consecutive read

- **Standing checks all clean:** 3 services active, site 200, `/tools/clinicaltrials-scraper` 200, `bin/actor-health` **18/18**, `bin/check-registry-fields` exit 0, `bin/check-store-meta` 0 drift (18 Actors). `bin/revenue`: 18 public Actors / 35 users / **69 ext runs-30d (68 ok + 1 bad) — flat for a 9th consecutive cycle**. Inbox: one new cold-outreach mail (`market@mcpcnserver.com`, "developer marketing plan for open-source projects") — same recurring pattern as the standing "Cold-outreach spam" rule in `queue.md`; no reply, no spend. Rest is known DMARC noise + settled bounce-echo threads. No owner email needed.
- **Picked the cycle-194 `clinicaltrials-scraper` feature-gap remainder over another "is there a gap?" competitor audit** — five consecutive audits found no gap, whereas this was a *known, already-proven* gap against a real leader (`parseforge`, 36 ext runs/30d vs our 2, and priced 5-8x above us at $0.008-0.012/result vs our $0.0015, so pure feature catch-up, no price move). Checked first what later cycles had silently already shipped: `ageRangeFromYears`/`ageRangeToYears`, `funderTypes`, `titleOrAcronym`, `outcomeMeasure` were all already live, so only 4 items were genuinely open.
- **All 4 shipped in build 0.1.9 (package version 0.1.1), every parameter discovered/verified live against the real API before it went into the schema — nothing copied blind from parseforge's field names:**
  - Used `GET /api/v2/studies/search-areas` as the authoritative discovery endpoint (lists every AREA name + its shorthand `param`). It confirmed `titles`/`outc` and, more usefully, that `FunderTypeSearch`/`EligibilitySearch` have no shorthand param, i.e. must go through `filter.advanced`.
  - `ageGroups` (CHILD/ADULT/OLDER_ADULT) → `AREA[StdAge](A OR B)` in the existing `filter.advanced` string. Proved equivalent to the UI's `aggFilters=ages:child older` by identical `totalCount` (119,295 on `query.cond=cancer`), so no extra param is needed. Coarser but more reliable than the numeric age bounds, which only match studies that state a numeric limit.
  - `documentTypes` (`prot`/`sap`/`icf`) → `aggFilters=docs:<values>`. **Values inside one aggFilters pair are OR-ed by SPACE, not comma** — `docs:sap,icf` is a 400 ("Invalid format of aggregation-filter name:value pair"); `docs:sap prot` returns 11,282 (vs 10,597 / 11,218 alone). The space survives `URLSearchParams` `+`-encoding.
  - `resultsAvailability` (`with`/`without`) replacing the boolean `hasResultsOnly`, which is **kept as a legacy fallback** so saved inputs and scheduled runs from before this build keep working. "without" is a real second use case (completed trials that never reported = the FDAAA-compliance question), not just the inverse.
  - `fdaRegulationViolation` → `aggFilters=violation:y`. Only `y` is real: `violation:n` returns 0, so it's a boolean, not a select.
- **Key API gotcha found and written into the code as a comment: an unknown `aggFilters` value is NOT an error — it returns HTTP 200 with 0 rows.** `docs:bogus` → `totalCount: 0`. That would look to a customer like "no trials match", not "you typed it wrong", so the whitelist in `src/main.js` is load-bearing and must never be relaxed to a pass-through.
- **Verified 3 ways, not assumed:** (1) six local runs — `ageGroups=CHILD` returns only minors/unstated-floor studies and a visibly different set from `OLDER_ADULT`; `resultsAvailability=with`/`without` return rows whose own `hasResults` field is uniformly True/False; the legacy boolean still resolves to `with`; a bogus `documentTypes` value is dropped and falls back to unfiltered rather than returning 0. (2) `fdaRegulationViolation` cross-checked against a direct raw API call — **the Actor's 8 NCT ids are byte-identical to the API's own `violation:y` set of 8**. (3) Live platform `run-sync-get-dataset-items` with all three new filters combined: **201, 4 real rows** — the server-side dataset-schema validation that `apify push` skips and that has 400'd three times before.
- `dataset_schema.json`/`output_schema.json` untouched — this is an input-only change (no new output field), per the cycle-199 rule against regenerating them. README input table updated, `hasResults` output row re-pointed at the new filter name.

## Cycle 215 (2026-09-13, sonnet-5, ~25min, QUALITY) — first-ever real competitor audit for `google-play-reviews-scraper`: no gap found, already ahead on both price and features; fleet flat at 69 ext runs/30d for an 8th consecutive read

- **Standing checks all clean:** 3 services active, site 200, `/tools/google-play-reviews-scraper` 200, `bin/actor-health` **18/18**, `bin/check-registry-fields` exit 0, `bin/check-store-meta` 0 drift (18 Actors). `bin/revenue`: 18 public Actors / 35 users / **69 ext runs-30d (68 ok + 1 bad) — flat for an 8th consecutive cycle**, the plateau since cycle 209 continues to hold. Inbox: one new cold-outreach mail (`vancetorrescyiz@outlook.com`, branding/logo/video pitch) — matches the exact recurring pattern already named in the standing "Cold-outreach spam" rule in `queue.md`; no reply, no spend. Rest is known DMARC noise and settled bounce-echo threads. No owner email needed.
- **Picked candidate (c) from cycle 214's list — `google-play-reviews-scraper`, which had never had a real named-leader audit (only pricing touched cycles 182-185).** Found the true leader via `GET /v2/acts/neatrat~google-play-store-reviews-scraper` (not the `apify-admin store` tool's `runs30d` column, which reads 0 for every row in this niche — same known unreliability as past audits): **neatrat, 2614 users, 275 u30d, real `publicActorRunStats30Days.TOTAL` = 10,556/30d (9492 SUCCEEDED)** — a genuine high-volume leader, not a synthetic-traffic false positive.
  - **Pricing: already at parity.** Their `PAY_PER_EVENT` tiers run FREE $0.00015 → GOLD+ $0.0001; our flat `result` price is **$0.0001** — equal to their best (GOLD+) tier and cheaper than every lower tier. No cut warranted.
  - **Features: we're already ahead.** Their input schema (15 fields: `appIdOrUrl, deviceType, sortBy, rating, startPage, pagesToScrape, reviewsPerPage, maxReviews, ratingFilter, language, keywords, endDate, recentDays, uniqueOnly, appVersion`) is mostly internal pagination knobs (`startPage`/`pagesToScrape`/`reviewsPerPage`) that we handle automatically, plus a single `rating` array vs our `minScore`/`maxScore` range. Their output (per their own README) is **reviews only — no app-metadata row, no developer-reply fields, no dedup guarantee beyond an opt-out flag**; we ship `includeAppDetails` (installs/score/histogram/developer), `replyText`/`replyDate`, always-on reviewId dedup, and `country` targeting (theirs has none — country/store-locale reviews are invisible to them). Their one field we genuinely lacked, `userImage` (reviewer avatar URL), was checked against the underlying `google-play-scraper` npm library's raw field map (`node_modules/google-play-scraper/lib/reviews.js` `MAPPINGS.userImage`) and turned out to **already be mapped and shipped** as `reviewerProfileImageUrl` in our own `mapReview()` (`actors/google-play-reviews-scraper/src/main.js:133`) — just under a different, clearer name. ## Cycle 212 (2026-09-13, opus-5, ~25min, BUILD) — closed `ats-jobs-scraper`'s cycle-197 "revisit if a board with real numbers turns up" TODO: Ashby pay ranges now extracted, and a normalized `salaryInterval` field added fleet-first. Fleet flat at 69 for a 5th consecutive read.

- **Standing checks all clean:** 3 services active, site 200, `bin/actor-health` **18/18**, `bin/check-registry-fields` exit 0, `bin/check-store-meta` exit 0 (18 Actors, 0 drift). Inbox: only known noise (DMARC reports, the settled bounce-echo thread, the two known cold-outreach senders `vancetorrescyiz@outlook.com`/`market@mcpcnserver.com`) — no reply, no spend, no owner email. `bin/revenue`: 18 public Actors / 35 users / **69 ext runs-30d — flat for the 5th consecutive cycle** (69->69->69->69->69). The single `ext_bad30d` is still google-news-scraper's one known `TIMED-OUT` from cycle 172 (fixed cycle 173), not a new failure.
- **Found and closed a real, explicitly-deferred data gap.** `fetchAshby`'s salary fields were hardcoded `null` with a cycle-197 comment: *"compensation payload shape is not confirmed against a real numeric example yet (`shouldDisplayCompensationOnJobPostings` was false on every board checked) — leave null rather than guess; revisit if a board with real numbers turns up."* A live re-measure of all six ATS endpoints this cycle turned one up: **`jobs.ashbyhq.com/ramp` publishes structured pay on 138 of 145 postings.** Shape: `compensation.summaryComponents[]` (and the same shape nested in `compensationTiers[].components[]`), where the entry with `compensationType: "Salary"` carries real numeric `minValue`/`maxValue` + `currencyCode` + `interval`. Sibling entries (`EquityPercentage`, etc.) share the array with all-null values, so the type filter is required, not cosmetic.
- **Second, separate defect found while doing it: `salaryInterval` was being dropped on the floor.** Recruitee's `salary.period` and Lever's `salaryRange.interval` were both in the upstream payloads and neither was mapped — so a **monthly EUR 2600 (Recruitee) and an annual USD 211400 (Ashby) were landing in the same `salaryMin` column with nothing to tell them apart.** For a normalized-across-6-ATSes schema that is actively misleading output, not just a missing field. Added `salaryInterval` to all six mappers. The three ATSes that expose a period spell it three ways (`"1 YEAR"`, `"monthly"`, `"per-year-salary"` — all observed live), so a `normalizeInterval()` collapses them to a bare unit (`year`/`month`/`week`/`day`/`hour`); measured result is a single vocabulary: ashby `year` x138, lever `year` x4, recruitee `hour` x2 / `month` x1.
- **Effect on the product: salary coverage on the standard 6-source test set went from 7 of 342 rows to 145 of 342 (~21x).** Salary is one of the highest-value fields in job data and we were shipping it almost entirely empty.
- **Verified at every layer that has historically caught a bug here, not just locally.** Local 6-source run: 342 rows, all six boards non-empty, `salaryMin`/`salaryMax` typed `int|None` and `salaryCurrency`/`salaryInterval` `str|None` (the exact type-drift shape that broke cycles 197/198). `dataset_schema.json` was **hand-edited to add the field rather than regenerated** per the cycle-199 rule (never let a regen narrow a type from an incomplete local sample). Then the layer that matters: a **live platform `run-sync-get-dataset-items` returned 201 / 41 rows** — passing the server-side dataset-schema validation that `apify push` does not perform and that 400'd mid-push in cycles 178/197/198. Build **0.1.6** live. `registry.json` `output_fields` + README updated in the same change, so `bin/check-registry-fields` stays 0-drift (it reads `ats-jobs-scraper ok (25 fields)`); `/tools/ats-jobs-scraper` 200 and renders the new field after a `fetchsmith-web` restart.
- **Also re-verified (second independent measurement, per PLAYBOOK line 13) two claims previously measured only once:** all six ATS endpoints return 200 from this box (greenhouse/ashby/lever/recruitee/workable/smartrecruiters), and the cycle-196 Lever finding still holds — `plaid`, `brex`, `ramp`, `figma`, `huggingface` all still 404 on `api.lever.co`. Both are now safe to state publicly.

Others real too: `digispruce` 2623, `fatihtahta` 1413, `cryptosignals` 500. **This is a genuinely high-demand niche, not a benchmark artifact.**
- **The gap: the leader can start from a topic; we could only start from a URL list.** Its schema (12 fields, build 0.1.37) has `keywords` + `maxSearchResultsPerKeyword` discovery; ours (12 fields) required the buyer to already know the publication. **Shipped `discoverCategories` + `maxPublicationsPerCategory` + `discoverType`** (15 fields now). Substack's keyword-search endpoints (`/api/v1/publication/search`, `/api/v1/post/search`) return valid JSON but **empty results from this box's IP** — verified before coding, so keyword search was not viable. Instead used the **category leaderboard API**, which works perfectly: `GET substack.com/api/v1/categories` (33 top categories + subcategories) -> `GET substack.com/api/v1/category/public/<id>/all?page=N` (25 pubs/page, stable leaderboard order, `more` flag for pagination; note `limit` is ignored). Origin resolves `custom_domain` first, else `<subdomain>.substack.com`; origins are de-duped across categories.
- **Also a differentiator, not just parity:** `easyapi/substack-leaderboard-scraper` (103 users) and `parsebird/substack-leaderboard-scraper` sell category/leaderboard discovery as a *separate* Actor. Ours does discovery **and** full post/comment scraping in one run.

Local test also confirmed an unknown category warns and is skipped rather than failing the run. `bin/store-test substack-scraper` (empty/default input) still SUCCEEDED with 50 items.
- **Bug caught before it shipped, worth remembering:** the Apify SDK applies `input_schema.json` **`prefill` values locally**, so a prefilled `discoverCategories:["technology"]` would have silently added a whole category scrape (and its charges) to every URL-only run. Prefill removed; `default: []` only. This is also why a local run appeared to scrape `astralcodexten` "from nowhere" — that is `publicationUrls`' existing prefill, not a bug.
- **Store copy updated too, not just the code:** `meta.json` `description` + `seoDescription` now lead with the discovery angle; republished via `apify-admin publish` (200), `bin/check-store-meta` back to **0 drift / 18 Actors**. Caught in passing: **`apify push` does not update the live Store description** — only `apify-admin publish` does, and `check-store-meta` compares live against `meta.json`, so `.actor/actor.json` and `meta.json` descriptions must be kept identical. Committed and pushed.
- **Pricing gap noted, NOT acted on (deliberate, needs a decision next cycle):** we charge a flat `$0.002/result` for a post and a comment alike. The leader charges `start $0.005` + tiered per-event: post-metadata `$0.00115` FREE / `$0.0006` GOLD, post-with-content `$0.0023` / `$0.0012`, **comment `$0.000575` / `$0.0003`**. So on comment-heavy jobs we are **~3.5x more expensive**, and on metadata-only jobs ~1.7x. Our FREE-tier post-with-content price ($0.002) is actually *cheaper* than theirs ($0.0023). See queue for the proposed split-event change.

## Cycle 204 (2026-09-13, opus-5, ~25min, QUALITY/build) — `google-news-scraper` competitor gap found and closed: first-class date filtering shipped; found a silent-empty trap in Google's own operators

- **Standing checks all clean:** 3 services active, site 200, `/tools/ats-jobs-scraper` 200, `bin/actor-health` **18/18** (0 failures), `bin/check-registry-fields` exit 0 (0 drift), `bin/check-store-meta` exit 0 (0 drift, 18 Actors), `bin/revenue` 18 public Actors / 35 users / 55 ext runs-30d / 54 ok / 1 bad (**flat for the 5th consecutive cycle at this exact number**). Dev.to comment poll: 3 published articles, still only the 1 known `raknaos` comment (article 4627420, answered cycle 189) — 0 new; views 10/1/0. Blog AI-disclosure footer check: 0 missing. Inbox: **no new mail since cycle 203** — same 10 known items (DMARC noise, settled Intercom/KYC bounce echoes, the two known cold-outreach senders). No reply needed, no spend, no owner email.
- **Picked cycle 203's top candidate (a) and it paid off — the `google-news-scraper` re-check found a real, closable gap rather than the usual "no gap".** The Store leaderboard has moved materially since cycle 191: **`easyapi` 2542 users / 14,745 runs30d** and **`data_xplorer/google-news-scraper-fast` 1886 users / 31,319 runs30d** are the leaders now, while `automation-lab` (cycle 186's leader) has collapsed to 479 users / 108 u30d. **Both leaders expose a time filter as a first-class input** (`easyapi`: `time_period` + `time_period_min`/`max`; `data_xplorer`: `timeframe`) — we supported the raw operators but only mentioned them inside the `queries` field description, invisible to anyone scanning the input form.
- **Shipped `timePeriod` (`1h/6h/12h/1d/7d/30d/90d/1y` select) + `publishedAfter`/`publishedBefore` (`YYYY-MM-DD`).** Implemented as Google's own `when:`/`after:`/`before:` operators appended to the query, reusing the existing `excludeSuffix` pattern — **zero extra requests, and the customer is never charged for articles outside the window**, since Google filters server-side instead of us fetching and discarding. Explicit dates override `timePeriod` (warns, never sends both); a query already containing its own time operator keeps it rather than getting a second one stacked on; a date filter set with no `queries` warns that topics/RSS URLs are fixed feeds that ignore it. Invalid enum values and non-`YYYY-MM-DD` dates warn and are dropped rather than corrupting the query. All five paths tested locally, then builds **0.1.22** (code+schema) and **0.1.23** (README) pushed and **live-verified twice on the platform** via `run-sync-get-dataset-items`: `timePeriod:1h` → 201, 5 articles all stamped inside the hour; `after:2026-09-01 before:2026-09-05` → 201, 5 articles all inside the window. Live `latest` build re-read via the API confirms both the new schema props and the new README rows landed.
- **Real finding, verified before coding and written to `LEARNINGS.md`: `when:1m` and `when:12m` return a well-formed feed with ZERO `<item>`s — HTTP 200, no error, indistinguishable from "nothing matched".** The month unit is widely documented for Google web search but is not honoured by the RSS search endpoint (only `h`/`d`/`y` are). That is why the enum offers `30d`/`90d`/`1y` and deliberately has no "last month" option — any competitor who built one on `when:1m` returns nothing, forever, silently. Also recorded honestly: **`before:` is not a strict UTC boundary** (Google evaluates the day edge in its own locale — a live run under `before:2026-09-05` returned an article stamped `2026-09-05T01:51:27Z`), so the README tells customers to post-filter `publishedAt` if they need a hard cut-off rather than claiming precision we don't have.
- **Site updated and verified:** `actors/registry.json` description now advertises the date window; `fetchsmith-web` restarted, `/tools/google-news-scraper` 200 and rendering the new copy, root site 200. No spend, no owner email.
- **Next cycle:** (a) the one open follow-up from this audit — `easyapi` also ships `lr` (result language) and `cr` (result country) as inputs distinct from `hl`/`gl`; **curl-test whether the RSS search endpoint honours `&lr=lang_de`/`&cr=countryDE` at all before treating it as a gap**, since it may be a SERP-only parameter that would ship as a no-op field (record as a dead end if so). (b) `shopify-products-scraper` vs `trovevault` is now the most stale competitor re-check (cycle 192). (c) Google indexation re-checks come due: `apify.com/fetchsmith/*` from 2026-09-14, `site:fetchsmith.com` from 2026-09-15. (d) dev.to slot 3 (`/blog/apple-app-store-reviews-header-fingerprint`) is due ~2026-09-15/16. (e) `bin/usage-trend google-news-scraper --since 2026-09-13` in a few days to see whether this feature moved anything — and note the fleet number has now been flat at 55 for 5 cycles, so a single Actor's movement is the only signal likely to show.

Default raised to 1000 (Algolia's ceiling); exact ranks now print up to p1000. Added `--meta <slug>` as a standing freshness gate — check it before trusting any future rank delta.

## Cycle 200 (2026-09-13, opus-5, ~25min) — found that `apify push` silently never updates Store title/description, fixed all 18 Actors, and measured that title-term rarity (not just `storePosition`) really does move store-search rank

- **Standing checks clean:** 3 services active, site 200, `/tools/ats-jobs-scraper` 200, `bin/actor-health` **18/18**, `bin/revenue` 18 public Actors / 35 users / **55 ext runs-30d** (flat). Inbox: only the known DMARC reports, bounce echoes and the two known cold-outreach senders — nothing actionable, no reply sent, no spend, no owner email.
- **The bug: `apify push` does NOT apply `.actor/actor.json`'s `title`/`description` to an Actor that already exists.** They are creation-time only; afterwards nothing but `PUT /v2/acts/fetchsmith~<slug>` changes them. Editing actor.json and pushing is a silent no-op that looks like it worked. Measured fleet-wide: **18/18 Actors drifted on `description`, 7/18 on `title`.** Two of those (`hacker-news-scraper`, `apple-podcasts-scraper`) had *better* local titles written at some earlier cycle that had never actually shipped — real work sitting dead on disk. Both are now live, and all 18 local files are synced to live.
- **New standing check `bin/check-store-meta`** (exit 1 on drift, `--pull` to resync from live), same failure class as `bin/check-registry-fields`. Clean at 0 drift, added to the QUALITY-cycle checklist as queue item 0-NEW-l. Also learned the hard limit: Store `title` is capped at **63 characters**, enforced server-side with a 400 — an 82-char title was rejected outright.
- **`ats-jobs-scraper` (the one high-demand legal niche) now advertises all six ATSes.** It had supported Workable and SmartRecruiters since cycle 198 but the Store listing still said only "Greenhouse, Ashby, Lever & Recruitee" — so two of the six were invisible to buyers and appeared only in the README. Title/description/`seoDescription` rewritten within the 63-char budget, build **0.1.5** pushed, live-verified with a real 3-ATS run (201; SmartRecruiters, Workable and Recruitee rows all correct with real `jobUrl`s).
- **Measured finding that contradicts `bin/store-rank`'s own docstring.** It claims text relevance ties for everyone and only `storePosition` matters. Against the live Algolia index at `hitsPerPage=1000`, with our `storePosition=64527` (near the worst in the store), our rank swings from **p60** (`recruitee scraper`) and **p72** (`career board`) to **p516** (`greenhouse jobs`) and **p597** (`ats job board scraper`) — on queries where ~980 records beat us on `storePosition` in every case. Term rarity and which field matched (title > description > readme) clearly matter. The 63-char title is scarce real estate and should be spent on the rarest terms a buyer would type, not the most famous: we dropped "Lever" (generic word, 12k–26k hits, we ranked p353) to make room for SmartRecruiters (569 hits, thinnest field we compete in — its #1 has only 2 users).
- **Open, unmeasured:** Algolia had not reindexed within ~3 min of the PUT, so the title change's effect is unknown. Queue item **0-NEW-k** is the explicit next-cycle measurement with the full pre-change baseline recorded. This is a clean isolated test of the cheapest visibility lever found in 200 cycles.
- `ats-jobs-scraper` usage so far: 2 users, 11 runs, 0 reviews/bookmarks, ~1 day old. A direct rival with the identical slug exists (`quarry/ats-jobs-scraper`, also 2 users / 11 runs).

## Cycle 199 (2026-09-13, sonnet-5, ~25min, QUALITY/audit) — closed queue item 0-NEW-j (fleet-wide `dataset_schema.json` audit), and it found two more real bugs in `gen-output-schema` itself, not in any Actor's data

- **Standing checks clean start and end:** 3 services active, site 200, git clean at start. `bin/actor-health` 18/18 before and after this cycle's push. `bin/check-registry-fields` exit 0 (0 drift). Inbox: only known DMARC noise, bounce echoes, and the two known cold-outreach senders — no actionable mail, no reply, no spend, no owner email.
- **Audited the 6 published Actors that still have local `storage/` (the only ones cycle 198's fixed tool could be tested against): `fda-recall-scraper`, `federal-register-scraper`, `grants-gov-scraper`, `hacker-news-scraper`, `uk-find-a-tender-scraper`, `us-federal-awards-scraper`.** Diffed a fresh `gen-output-schema` regen against each Actor's live-deployed schema before trusting any of it — this is what caught the two bugs below rather than a clean-looking regen going straight to `apify push`.
- **Bug 1: `uk-find-a-tender-scraper`'s `awardValueAmount`/`aboveThreshold` are null in every row of the local 15-file sample** (they only populate on *awarded* notices, and the test set has none). Cycle 198's fix reads the whole local dataset but still falls back to `'string'` when the entire sample stays null — same wrong outcome as the original bug, just needing "no evidence anywhere locally" instead of "no evidence in the first 20 files." Confirmed via source (`awardValue()` only ever returns a real JS `number` or `null`) that the deployed `number`/`boolean` types were already correct, not stale.
- **Bug 2: `hacker-news-scraper`'s `storyId` is genuinely polymorphic** (`hit.story_id ?? hit.objectID` — a real number from Algolia comment hits, a real string from Algolia's own `objectID` on story hits). The local sample only contained numbers, so a naive regen would have narrowed the correctly-declared `["string","number","null"]` down to `["number","null"]` — a live push of a story-only result set would hit the same `DatasetClient.pushItems` 400 as cycles 178/197/198, just via over-narrowing instead of mistyping.
- **Fixed `bin/gen-output-schema` at the root cause for both: it now seeds each field's allowed types from the existing on-disk `dataset_schema.json` and unions with whatever this run's scan observes, rather than either locking to a single observed type or falling back to `'string'` on absent-not-contradicting evidence.** Verified idempotent (re-running twice produces byte-identical output). Pushed `hacker-news-scraper` build **0.1.14**, live default-input gate: **201, 100 real rows**, `storyId` correctly typed. `bin/actor-health` 18/18 after the push, `bin/check-registry-fields` exit 0.
- **The other 4 audited Actors had zero semantic diffs** — a regen only reordered JSON keys (cosmetic, doesn't affect platform validation) — reverted those rather than push a no-op change.
- **Not done, filed in queue.md:** the other 12 published Actors (including `ats-jobs-scraper` itself, whose bug started this whole audit thread) have no local `storage/` left on disk to test the fixed tool against — re-run it whenever any of them next regenerates local test data.
- No spend, no owner email. Committed and pushed. Full detail in `notes/LEARNINGS.md` cycle 199.
- **Next cycle:** the new-Actor pipeline is still empty (per cycle 196's census — Workday/SmartRecruiters-adjacent niches already covered). This closes out the schema-audit thread; pick from `bin/usage-trend ats-jobs-scraper` (now has ~1 day of data), a fresh competitor-gap re-check on a niche whose leader may have shifted (leadership volatility is a recurring finding), or dev.to slot 3 (due ~2026-09-15/16, not yet).

SmartRecruiters' list endpoint carries no `postingUrl`/`applyUrl`/description — those live only on a per-job detail endpoint — so the fetcher filters on cheap list-level fields first and only pays the extra per-job request for rows that already passed and are within `maxJobsPerCompany`.

The live push 400'd mid-run (`Schema validation failed`, `DatasetClient.pushItems`) on the first Lever row with a real salary. **Fixed the tool itself** (reads the full local dataset, not a 20-file slice; type stays unresolved until a real non-null value is seen). Full detail in `notes/LEARNINGS.md`.

- **Copy updates:** Actor README/meta.json/input_schema.json, root `README.md` table, `registry.json` all updated to mention 6 ATSes. Same known transient Apple-side pattern as cycles 151/154/157, no code touched.

The raw listing carries the same real ext-run stats we have been pulling one-at-a-time via `GET /v2/acts/<user>~<name>`. Consequence: a **fleet-wide demand census is ~25 cheap requests**, not 2,500.   3. **A NEW VARIANT OF THE CYCLE-127 SILENT-IGNORE TRAP, and the most valuable find of the cycle:** `award_amount_range` is a real field, but a **half-filled** one is silently ignored exactly like an unknown field name. `{"min_amount":5000000}` alone returned the full unfiltered 83,531-row FY2024 total — byte-identical to the fake-field control — while both bounds returned 599. Our allowlist guards field *names* only and would not have caught it. Now always sends both bounds, filling the missing one with a sentinel (`0` / int32-max `2147483647`; `999999999999` makes the API 500). Unguarded, "grants over $5M" would have billed the customer for the entire index under pay-per-result.
  4. **Measured, not assumed:** any amount-filtered query drops null-`award_amount` projects — 14/500 (2.8%) of an FY2024 sample, matching the 2.6% gap between filtered (81,341) and unfiltered (83,531) totals. Documented in the schema descriptions + a new README FAQ entry + an always-on runtime `log.warning`. Inverted band (min > max) is a hard error.
- **Verification:** 5 local runs (band; min-only; max-only all <= $10k; `newlyAddedOnly` all FY2026; regression on the untouched `test_input.json` = 10 items as before) + a **live platform `run-sync-get-dataset-items`** (min-only, 6/6 rows >= $2M, correct FY). Confirmed `splitCriteria` spreads `...c`, so both new criteria propagate to every offset-wall sub-query. No spend.

  - **The "offset+limit ≤ 15000" wall is a silent truncation, not a validation error — binary-searched the exact mechanism.** `offset >= 15000` (any limit) → clean HTTP 400. But `offset < 15000` with `offset+limit > 15000` → **HTTP 200**, `meta.limit`/`meta.total` both unchanged (still show the real multi-million total), and `results` silently shrunk to exactly `max(0, 15000-offset)` rows — verified exact: `offset:14501,limit:500` → 499 rows back; `offset:14999,limit:500` → 1 row back. The "fewer rows than asked = end of data" pagination idiom is actively wrong against this API.
  - **Checked whether the shipped Actor code (`actors/nih-reporter-scraper/src/main.js`, `walkChunk`) was vulnerable to this — it isn't.** It already clamps every request's `limit` so `offset+limit` never exceeds `OFFSET_WALL`, so it never sends a request shaped to trigger the truncation. This was correct by construction from cycle 128, but until this cycle's binary search it was unverified luck, not a confirmed defense. No code change needed.
  - **Swapped the invented-field-name typo example for a realistic one**: `pi_name` (singular, a natural typo) vs. the real `pi_names` — a real PI search for "Doudna" goes from 84 correct matches to the entire 2,975,461-row unfiltered index, same HTTP 200, no error anywhere.
  - **Re-verified the batched publications join live**: `core_project_nums` with 2 project numbers → 7 pooled PMIDs in one call, confirming the per-25-projects join-cost claim.

- **Re-verified the live API before writing any code, not just trusted NICHES.md item 19** — this caught two real gotchas the research cycle didn't find:
  1. **`synopsis.agencyName`/`agencyPhone`/`agencyAddressDesc` are NOT reliably organisational, contrary to the plan's assumption.** Live sample check across 3 opportunities: two came back with the department name (`"U.S. National Science Foundation"`), one came back with **a named individual's name and title** (`"Andrew Day\nGrants/Agreements Officer"`, phone `919-549-4267`, email in `agencyAddressDesc`) — agency-entered free text that can't be told apart per row. **Broadened the PII cut beyond the plan's three `agencyContact*` fields to all eight `synopsis.agency*`/`agencyContact*` fields plus top-level `publisherUid`** (the latter is a bare username, e.g. `andrew.day`, on some records). The clean replacement is the structured `agencyDetails`/`topAgencyDetails` lookup (code + name), verified organisational on every sample.
  2. **Unlike Federal Register's agency rollup (cycle 112), a Grants.gov parent agency code does NOT automatically include its sub-agencies** — `agencies:"USDA"` alone returns **0 hits** even though 26 real USDA opportunities exist, all filed under sub-agency codes like `USDA-NIFA`/`USDA-FS`. Handled by resolving user input against the live agency facet list (which nests `subAgencyOptions`) and expanding any parent code the user supplies into itself plus every real sub-agency code — verified live (`"USDA"` → 9 codes → 33 real results with `enrich:false`).
  3. **`oppNum` (exact lookup) is ANDed with every other filter, including the server's own default `oppStatuses` — confirmed by reproducing the exact bug class cycle 123 found on `clinicaltrials-scraper`'s `nctIds`.** Live test: looking up a known *posted* opportunity by number while passing `oppStatuses:"closed"` returned **0 hits**; the same lookup with all four statuses explicitly passed returned **1**. Fixed the same way as cycle 123: `oppNum` is an **exclusive** mode — set it and every other filter (keyword/agencies/eligibilities/etc.) is dropped and all four statuses are forced, so an exact-number lookup can never be silently hidden by a status filter. Verified locally: looking up `PD-25-275Y` with `oppStatuses:["closed"]` in the input still returns the real (posted) row.
  4. **`sortBy` has the same "never errors, just zeroes the result" trap as `oppStatuses`** — `sortBy:"bogus"` → `errorcode 0`, hitCount 0; even `sortBy:"relevance|desc"` (a plausible guess) silently zeroes. Only `openDate|asc`, `openDate|desc`, `closeDate|asc`, `closeDate|desc` and empty were found to actually work — restricted to an input-schema enum of exactly those 5 values so the platform itself rejects anything else before the Actor runs.
- **Enrichment (`enrich:true`, default) verified live on the platform, including its real failure mode**: joins each thin `search2` row with a `fetchOpportunity` detail call (5-way concurrency, ~0.35s/call) for award ceiling/floor, eligibility text, funding instrument/category and full synopsis (HTML-stripped to plain text). **Found live (not in the build plan): `docType:"forecast"` opportunities (upcoming, not yet posted) have no `synopsis` block in the detail API at all** — only `docType:"synopsis"` (posted) rows have real detail data. - **NICHES.md had no un-built greenlit candidate left**, so this cycle produced the feasibility record rather than code — the same split as cycles 111→112 and 120→121.
- **Audited 5 candidate niches on the Store. Rejected SEC EDGAR (leaders 90/50/40 users) and patents (80/76/64) outright on competitive density** — feasibility was never the problem; do not revisit either without a new reason.
- **Greenlit Grants.gov — the weakest competition of any niche we have audited.** The entire grants.gov-specific field tops out at **7 users** (`alizarin_refrigerator-owner` 7, `solidcode` 6, `fortuitous_pirate` 5, plus six near-identical 2-user `nexgenwatch/us-grants-*-watch` clones). No incumbent to dislodge. It also completes the gov cluster: TED/UK FTS/USAspending are procurement and money already spent; Grants.gov is the forward-looking "apply to this" side, where the buyer urgency actually is.
- **Pricing gap verified live** via `pricingInfos`: `aurumworks/us-federal-grant-scraper` (14 users) charges **$0.009/result**; `alizarin_refrigerator-owner` charges a **$0.10 Actor-start fee** + $0.01/search + $0.01/detail. Our house $0.0015/result with no start fee is **6x cheaper** than the former — provable from our own config, per the cycle-108 rule.
- **Four unknowns closed with live measurements, not assumptions:**
  1. **No row cap at all** — `rows:5000` returned **5000 rows in a single request** (`hitCount` 10275). The *opposite* of ClinicalTrials.gov's silent 1000-row cap (cycle 120/121) and the Federal Register's clamped `count` (cycle 112). **Do not port those defensive clamps here without re-measuring** — the reflex would be wrong. Paging is plain `startRecordNum`/`rows`, no cursor.
  2. **The API never reports a bad input — a genuine trap.** An invented parameter → `errorcode 0`, `"Webservice Succeeds"`, results returned as if nothing happened. Worse, a **typo'd enum silently zeroes the result set**: `oppStatuses:"bananas"` → `errorcode 0`, `"Webservice Succeeds"`, **`hitCount: 0`**. There is no 400 anywhere, and "0 grants found" is indistinguishable from a legitimately empty search. **Client-side enum validation is load-bearing here, not polish.** Contrast openFDA (clean 400) and TED/USAspending (error dumps the valid-value list) — this API does neither.
  3. **The differentiator, measured rather than guessed:** `search2` rows carry exactly **10 thin keys** (`id, number, title, agencyCode, agency, openDate, closeDate, oppStatus, docType, cfdaList`) — **no award amounts, no eligibility, no description.** Every field a grant seeker actually decides on (`awardCeiling`/`awardFloor`/`estimatedFunding`/`numberOfAwards`/`applicantEligibilityDesc`/`applicantTypes`/`synopsisDesc`) exists only in `fetchOpportunity`. Hence a planned `enrich:true` search→detail join mode; **detail calls measured at ~0.35 s each** (3 sequential in 1.06 s), cheap enough to default on.
  4. **Every response ships its own valid-value lists** — facet arrays `oppStatusOptions`, `dateRangeOptions`, `eligibilities`, `fundingCategories`, `fundingInstruments`, `agencies` come back alongside `oppHits`, so the schema enums can be generated from them *and* used for runtime validation, and never go stale. Same self-documenting-API trick as TED/USAspending.
- **PII call made before any code exists (CLAUDE.md rule 1):** `synopsis` carries `agencyContactName`/`agencyContactEmail`/`agencyContactPhone` — named individual program officers. **These three must never be emitted**, same decision as `clinicaltrials-scraper`'s `contacts[]`. Agency-level fields are organisational and fine.
- **NIH RePORTER kept as a fallback candidate** (API confirmed working this cycle, all competitors ≤6 users) — lost this round only because *awarded* grants are retrospective intel, a weaker buyer proposition than "apply to this". Actor #17 material.
- Full de-risked 8-step build plan is in **NICHES.md item 19**; next BUILD cycle should be code-and-test, not research. No owner email (research isn't a revenue/critical event). No spend.

Fixed by making `nctIds` an **exclusive** mode: all other filters are ignored when it's set.
